This deck walks the whole Tandem repository: what the product is, how the packages fit, how a request moves through the code, what every file does, and which optimizations were made with their measured results.

What Tandem is

Team chat that you host yourself

Tandem (formerly SlackOSS) is an MIT-licensed, self-hosted team chat with channels, DMs, threads, files, search, huddles and Slack-compatible integrations. One TypeScript server with Node's built-in SQLite keeps a whole workspace in one data folder. It runs as a standalone Node bundle, in Docker, or inside the Electron desktop app, so anyone can host a workspace from their own PC and share it over the LAN or a Cloudflare tunnel. A shared React UI powers both the desktop app and a browser client that the server serves itself.

Packages · 1–4 of 7

What each package is for

packages/protocol

@slackoss/protocol

Shared types and zod schemas for entities, REST bodies, WebSocket events, search syntax, permissions and mDNS discovery. Defines constants such as PROTOCOL_VERSION, DEFAULT_PORT 8543 and SEND_RETRY_WINDOW_MS.

packages/server

@slackoss/server

The workspace server: Fastify REST routes (server.ts), the WebSocket Gateway (gateway.ts), the SQLite Store (store.ts) with migrations (db.ts), backup/restore/recover tools, integrations, outbound-request guards, rate limits and mDNS. createWorkspaceServer() is used by the CLI, Docker and the desktop app alike.

packages/client-core

@slackoss/client-core

Framework-free client SDK: a REST wrapper (api.ts), a resilient WebSocket WorkspaceClient that keeps a zustand replica, the optimistic outbox, drafts, file cache, notification rules and the WebRTC huddle engine. It replays missed events by seq after reconnecting.

packages/ui

@slackoss/ui

The React interface shared by desktop and web: App.tsx (join screen vs workspace session), the WorkspaceScreen with Sidebar, MessageTimeline, Composer and ThreadPanel, dialogs for hosting, people, apps and search, and huddle views. A Platform abstraction (webPlatform or the Electron preload bridge) supplies storage, downloads, LAN discovery and hosting.

Packages · 5–7 of 7

What each package is for

apps/web

@slackoss/web

Thin browser entry that renders <App platform={webPlatform()} />. Its Vite build is the browser client that every server serves at its root URL.

apps/desktop

@slackoss/desktop

The Tandem Electron app. The main process runs the hosting controller (hosting.ts and registry.ts embed createWorkspaceServer), the cloudflared tunnel manager (tunnel.ts), mDNS browsing, encrypted saved sign-ins, settings and outbox storage, backup workers, the tray and tandem:// deep links. The renderer hosts the shared UI.

apps/server-cli

slackoss-server

Bundles the server and the built web client into one runnable file (slackoss-server.js) using tsup. It provides the CLI: run, backup, verify-backup, restore and recover, with flags such as --invite-only, --public-url and --retention-days.

Running it

Ways to run a Tandem workspace

Desktop host (Electron)

From the Join screen, 'Host a workspace on this computer' runs the same createWorkspaceServer inside the Electron main process, with data in <userData>/hosted/w-<id>/. Teammates join over the LAN (mDNS or ip:port) while the app keeps running, minimized to the tray.

Desktop host + Cloudflare tunnel / own address

'Open to all' spawns cloudflared for a temporary trycloudflare.com HTTPS address with invite-only on by default, and closing the link ends it. A stable public address can come from Tailscale Funnel, a reverse proxy, or a Tandem-managed Cloudflare connector set under 'Your own address'.

Standalone server (VPS or spare machine)

Run node slackoss-server.js --data ./data --name "My Team" --invite-only on Node 24+. It is a single bundled file with zero dependencies that also serves the browser client, and HTTPS comes from a reverse proxy such as Caddy with --public-url set.

Docker

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build runs the server as a non-root user with data in the slackoss-data volume and GET /api/health for health checks. The supplied Compose file requires invites, and a reverse proxy goes in front for HTTPS.

Browser client

Every server serves the full web client at http://host:8543/, built from apps/web with precompressed Brotli/gzip assets. Browsers need HTTPS (or localhost) for microphone access in huddles.

Glossary · 1 of 5

Terms you will meet in the code

Workspace

One server instance with one data folder (workspace.db plus files/). It has a permanent ULID workspace_id in meta that survives renames and restores.

Event log / seq

Every mutation appends a row to the events table with a monotonically increasing seq and is fanned out over WebSocket. The newest 20,000 events are kept for clients to resync against.

lastSeq watermark / replay

The highest seq a client has applied. Its hello carries lastSeq, the gateway replays everything after it, and a client that has fallen off the log takes a fresh 'ready' snapshot instead.

Ready snapshot

The handshake reply with users, visible channels, memberships, presence, saved items, thread follows, mention counts, huddles, workspaceId and friends.

Local replica

The zustand store inside WorkspaceClient that the UI renders from immediately. It is updated by HTTP responses and socket events.

Outbox / pending message

Optimistic sends waiting to reach the server, capped at 50 per account. They are persisted per workspace and account and merged across windows using revisions and tombstones.

Glossary · 2 of 5

Terms you will meet in the code

Send key (nonce)

A random id attached to each send. The server's message_requests table maps (user, nonce) to one message, so retries and restored outboxes never create duplicates, and a different body under the same key returns 409…

Publish after commit

Changes are written in one SQLite transaction and only then published to sockets (publishCommitted). If fan-out fails, sockets are closed so clients reconnect and replay.

Gateway / audience

The WebSocket hub that decides who may see each event: public-channel events go to everyone, while private channels and DMs go only to current members.

Read cursors

Per-channel last_read_seq and replies_read_seq on membership, plus per-thread last_read_seq in thread_follows. 'Mark unread' moves a cursor back.

Thread following

Writing a thread's root or a reply auto-follows it. Followed threads appear in Threads with unread counts but notify only through the channel's notify level.

Notify level / DND

Per-channel notifications are all, mentions or nothing, plus a mute. Do Not Disturb snoozes notifications per user. decideNotification gives a reason for each decision.

Tandem codebase tour · The big picture

22 / 340

Send key (nonce): A random id attached to each send. The server's message_requests table maps (user, nonce) to one message, so retries and restored outboxes never create duplicates, and a different body under the same key returns 409 nonce_conflict. Publish after commit: Changes are written in one SQLite transaction and only then published to sockets (publishCommitted). If fan-out fails, sockets are closed so clients reconnect and replay. Gateway / audience: The WebSocket hub that decides who may see each event: public-channel events go to everyone, while private channels and DMs go only to current members. Read cursors: Per-channel last_read_seq and replies_read_seq on membership, plus per-thread last_read_seq in thread_follows. 'Mark unread' moves a cursor back. Thread following: Writing a thread's root or a reply auto-follows it. Followed threads appear in Threads with unread counts but notify only through the channel's notify level. Notify level / DND: Per-channel notifications are all, mentions or nothing, plus a mute. Do Not Disturb snoozes notifications per user. decideNotification gives a reason for each decision.

Glossary · 3 of 5

Terms you will meet in the code

Huddle

A live audio/video/screen room attached to a channel or DM. It is a WebRTC mesh signalled by the gateway, exists only in memory and ends when everyone leaves.

Claim code / owner

The first account on a fresh server becomes owner. Registering from a non-local machine needs the claim code printed at startup.

Invite-only / invite code

With --invite-only, accounts after the owner need a code. Codes expire and can be limited, revoked, and paused when their creator loses permission.

Hosted workspace registry

The desktop settings.json list of workspaces hosted on this computer: folder, workspace id, cached name and port, and last hosted time. Folders are random (w-<hex>) rather than named after the workspace.

Open to all

The desktop control that exposes a hosted workspace publicly through a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel or a configured stable address.

Isolated start

--isolated runs a restored copy on localhost only, sending no scheduled messages or app events and making no mDNS announcement, so a backup can be inspected safely.

Glossary · 4 of 5

Terms you will meet in the code

workspace.lock

An OS file lock that ensures only one server process opens a data directory. restore and recover are refused while it is held.

Pre-upgrade copy

Before a schema-changing migration, the server snapshots workspace.db into pre-upgrade/ and keeps the newest three copies.

Tombstone (message)

A deleted message keeps its id, author and timestamp but no content. Copies of its text are also redacted from the event log and queued app deliveries.

Retention sweep

Optional --retention-days hourly job that permanently removes older conversation in bounded passes, treating each thread as one unit.

Scheduled message

A server-side 'send later' queue item that sends even if the author's app is closed. Its status moves between queued, held, failed and sent.

App / bot / xoxb token

A Slack-compatible integration with a bot user and a hashed bot token. It supports chat.postMessage, auth.test and views.open, plus webhooks, slash commands, buttons and modals.

Glossary · 5 of 5

Terms you will meet in the code

Signed outbound request

Requests to apps carry v0=HMAC-SHA256 signatures in both x-slack-signature and x-slackoss-signature. Private-network targets are refused unless --allow-private-hooks is set.

Event delivery queue

The durable, ordered per-subscription outbound queue (event_deliveries). It retries 8 times, holds at most 500 per endpoint, and receivers deduplicate by event_id.

Download ticket

A single-use, session-bound token valid for 60 seconds that lets the browser or OS download manager stream a large file without the bearer header.

Storage budget

The optional --storage-limit-mb cap covering stored and in-flight uploads. Uploads over the cap get 507, and abandoned uploads are freed after 24 hours.

workspaceStorageKey

The device-storage scope (baseUrl, workspaceId, selfId, kind) for drafts, outbox and recent searches. It keeps local work attached to a workspace across address changes once the new address is approved.

Platform

The UI's abstraction over the host environment: webPlatform uses IndexedDB and iframe downloads, while the desktop preload bridge provides IPC for storage, LAN discovery and hosting.

Flow 1 of 8

Sending a message

1

Composer (packages/ui) calls WorkspaceClient.send(); a leading /word is run as a slash command instead

2

client-core generates a random 16-byte nonce (send key) and adds an optimistic PendingMessage to state.pending, the outbox, which is capped at 50 per account

3

deliver() uploads any attachments first via POST /api/channels/:id/files, then calls POST /api/channels/:id/messages with {text, nonce, threadRootId?, fileIds?}

4

server.ts rations the request per account, checks channel access and archival, then postMessage() runs in one store.transaction

5

Inside the transaction: a repeated nonce returns the existing message (or 409 nonce_conflict); otherwise createMessage, attachFiles, recordMessageRequest, and recordEvent append 'message.created' to the events log with a new seq. The FTS5 trigger indexes the text and auto-follows the thread for replies

6

After commit, publishCommitted() calls gateway.publish() to fan the event envelope out to every socket allowed to see the channel, queues app event deliveries, and pushes thread-follow states and mention counts

7

The sender's client applies the HTTP response and reconciles the pending entry by nonce; other clients' WorkspaceClient.applyEvent() updates their replica and advances lastSeq

8

MessageTimeline re-renders from the zustand store, and notify.ts decides whether to raise a notification

Flow 2 of 8

Signing in and connecting a session

1

JoinScreen probes the server with GET /api/server-info, then calls POST /api/auth/login, or POST /api/auth/register with an optional inviteCode or claimCode

2

The server checks the scrypt password hash (register: the first account becomes owner; --invite-only consumes an invite; non-local owner claims need the printed claim code)

3

The server creates a random 32-byte session token and stores only its SHA-256 hash in sessions, with a device label and an expiry

4

The client saves the server and token (desktop: encrypted with Electron safeStorage; web: device storage) and App.tsx opens a WorkspaceClient

5

WorkspaceClient opens /ws and sends hello {token, protocolVersion, lastSeq, syncVersion: 1}

6

The gateway validates the token hash, refuses a protocol mismatch (4002), an invalid session (4003) or a pending password change (4004), and replies with a 'ready' snapshot of users, visible channels, memberships, presence, saved items, thread follows, mention counts, huddles, workspaceId and friends

7

If lastSeq is still in the log, the missed events are replayed followed by 'synced'; otherwise the client resets from the snapshot. Bearer tokens authenticate all REST calls

Flow 3 of 8

Joining a workspace (LAN discovery, direct address or invite link)

1

A hosting server advertises itself over mDNS as service type 'slackoss' with TXT {name, ver, proto, inst}, unless started with --no-mdns or --isolated

2

In the desktop app, the main process browses with bonjour-service and the Join screen reads the list through the lan:snapshot IPC call

3

Alternatively the user types ip:port or a hostname, or opens an invite link: http://host:8543/#/join/<code> in a browser, or tandem://join?host=...&code=... (older slackoss:// links still work) in the desktop app

4

Owners and admins (and members granted can_invite) create codes with POST /api/invites; codes expire after 7 days in the dialog and can be revoked

5

The Join screen prefills the invite code; registration consumes one use of the invite inside the same transaction that creates the user

6

The session then connects exactly as in the sign-in flow

Flow 4 of 8

Hosting from the desktop app and opening it to the internet

1

Join screen > 'Host a workspace on this computer' > HostDialog calls hosting:start over IPC

2

hosting.ts creates a new folder hosted/w-<32 hex> and a registry entry in settings.json, then calls createWorkspaceServer in the Electron main process; the server writes workspace_id as a ULID in meta

3

The registry records the workspace id and bound port; older slug-named folders are adopted read-only on launch

4

LAN teammates discover it over mDNS or connect to ip:port; the server also serves the browser client

5

'Open to all' (hosting:openToAll) makes tunnel.ts spawn cloudflared for a Quick Tunnel and parse the https://…trycloudflare.com address, verifies the address reaches this workspace, and keeps invite-only on by default; the server trusts the visitor-address header only from loopback while the tunnel is live

6

Alternatively a stable address (Tailscale Funnel, reverse proxy, or a Tandem-managed Cloudflare connector) is set as the public URL used in invite links

7

Closing the window moves Tandem to the tray while hosting; stopping or quitting asks first, then ends the tunnel and the server stops cleanly

Flow 5 of 8

Huddle (WebRTC call)

1

WorkspaceClient.joinHuddle() fetches ICE servers from the authenticated GET /api/rtc-config (empty by default, so LAN only)

2

The client sends huddle.join {channelId, requestId} over the socket; the Gateway admits it to an in-memory room (never written to the event log) and broadcasts huddle.participants to the channel audience

3

huddle.ts opens one RTCPeerConnection per other participant (mesh). The offerer creates three transceivers (mic, camera, screen), which the answerer adopts

4

SDP and ICE are exchanged as huddle.signal messages, which the gateway relays only between two people in the same room who can both access the channel

5

Media flows peer-to-peer or through a configured TURN relay; mute and camera state are signalled explicitly. huddle.leave, or a closed socket, removes the participant

Flow 6 of 8

File upload and download

1

Composer attachments upload through XHR multipart to POST /api/channels/:id/files with progress events

2

The server streams the part to data/files/<fileId>, reserving bytes in StorageBudget as they arrive; going over --storage-limit-mb returns 507 storage_quota_exceeded and leaves nothing behind. A files row is created without a message_id

3

The message send then attaches the fileIds in the same transaction; files never attached are swept after 24 hours unless a scheduled message holds them (scheduled_files)

4

Small files are fetched with the bearer token into the client FileCache for previews; files of 8 MiB or more request POST /api/files/:id/download-token and receive a single-use ticket that expires in 60 s and is tied to the session

5

The browser or desktop download manager opens GET /api/files/:id?download=<ticket>; the server re-checks access and streams the file

6

Deleting a message removes file rows in the transaction and queues pending_file_deletions; a background worker removes the blobs and retries on failure

Flow 7 of 8

Backup and restore

1

CLI: slackoss-server backup --data ./data --out <dir> writes a consistent SQLite snapshot (including the WAL), every referenced attachment and manifest.json (schema version, checksums, row counts), staged and verified beside the destination

2

verify-backup checks checksums, attachment paths, schema, foreign keys and row counts, and lists what the backup would contact (app URLs, queued scheduled messages, undelivered events, accepted sign-ins)

3

restore verifies, stages and re-verifies, then swaps the backup in and renames the old directory to data.superseded-<timestamp>. It is refused while a server holds workspace.lock or when the backup comes from a newer schema

4

--isolated starts a copy on 127.0.0.1 that sends no scheduled messages and contacts no apps or mDNS, so a backup can be inspected safely

5

Desktop: Back up now, Automatic backups (daily or weekly with retention and backoff) and Restore from a backup run in a worker thread; a restored workspace is held until 'Put back in use'

6

Before any schema-changing upgrade, the server copies workspace.db into pre-upgrade/ and keeps the 3 most recent copies

Flow 8 of 8

Offline outbox recovery and reconnect

1

When the socket drops, WorkspaceClient shows status 'reconnecting' and retries with exponential backoff (1 s doubling to 30 s)

2

Unsent messages stay in state.pending; DraftPersistence writes outboxSnapshot() to device storage under workspaceStorageKey(baseUrl, workspaceId, selfId, 'outbox') (desktop: merged in the main process; web: IndexedDB transactions) as a merge of puts and tombstones across windows

3

After a restart, restoreOutbox() puts the entries back and re-delivers them with the same nonce, so the server's message_requests table settles a repeat onto the same message instead of a duplicate

4

Entries with attachments, sends older than SEND_RETRY_WINDOW_MS (30 days) and earlier refusals wait for the author's Retry instead

5

On reconnect, hello carries lastSeq; the gateway replays events since then (the log keeps the newest 20,000), or the client takes a fresh snapshot when it has fallen off the log

Area 1 of 14 · packages/protocol

Protocol: the shared language

The shared contract between the Tandem server and all clients, published as TypeScript source (no build) under the name @slackoss/protocol. entities.ts and events.ts define the data model and every WebSocket message; rest.ts holds zod schemas the server validates HTTP input with; search.ts, format.ts, discovery.ts, huddle.ts and permissions.ts hold small pure helpers both sides must agree on. index.ts re-exports everything, and a ./rest subpath exposes the schemas alone. Three vitest files cover the logic-bearing helpers.

36 / 340

Protocol: the shared language. The shared contract between the Tandem server and all clients, published as TypeScript source (no build) under the name @slackoss/protocol. entities.ts and events.ts define the data model and every WebSocket message; rest.ts holds zod schemas the server validates HTTP input with; search.ts, format.ts, discovery.ts, huddle.ts and permissions.ts hold small pure helpers both sides must agree on. index.ts re-exports everything, and a ./rest subpath exposes the schemas alone. Three vitest files cover the logic-bearing helpers.

Protocol: the shared language · 1–2 of 9 smaller files

entities.ts and rest.ts

entities.ts

Core data model types · 475 lines

Defines the shared shapes of everything the server stores and sends: users, channels, messages, files, invites, apps, integrations, audit entries, scheduled messages, thread follows and workspace status. It is almost entirely TypeScript interfaces and type unions, plus a few constants. Both the server and every client agree on data through these types.

  • IDs are ULID-style sortable strings; Message.text is Slack-mrkdwn-compatible
  • Message carries seq (event-log position used for unread math), nonce (idempotency key), broadcast flag for replies also shown in the channel, and app buttons (MessageAction)

rest.ts

REST request validation schemas · 312 lines

Holds the zod schemas the server uses to validate HTTP request bodies and query strings, and the inferred TypeScript types clients use to build them. It covers auth, profile, channels, messages, scheduling, search, history paging, invites, admin actions and every integration endpoint. Limits (lengths, counts, page sizes) live here so both sides share them.

  • Handles: 2-32 chars, lowercase letters, digits, . _ -
  • Messages: up to 12000 chars and 10 file ids; must have text or files (refine)

Optimization: Page sizes are capped (e.g. history 200, search 100, saved 100) to bound query cost

packages/protocol/src/entities.ts (475 lines, changed in 32 commits, added 2026-08-31, last changed 2026-10-02). Defines the shared shapes of everything the server stores and sends: users, channels, messages, files, invites, apps, integrations, audit entries, scheduled messages, thread follows and workspace status. It is almost entirely TypeScript interfaces and type unions, plus a few constants. Both the server and every client agree on data through these types. How it works: - IDs are ULID-style sortable strings; Message.text is Slack-mrkdwn-compatible - Message carries seq (event-log position used for unread math), nonce (idempotency key), broadcast flag for replies also shown in the channel, and app buttons (MessageAction) - ThreadFollow has a revision counter so late echoes cannot undo newer changes, plus an optional unreadHold - WorkspaceStatus is the owner/admin ops view: DB/WAL bytes, attachment removal queue, deliveries, scheduled queue, retention, sockets, event-loop delay and background failures, with no message content - PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1; SEND_RETRY_WINDOW_MS = 30 days, kept here so importing it does not pull in zod - Many optional fields are documented as absent from older servers, for backward compatibility Key exports: ID, User, Role, Channel, ChannelType, ChannelPrefs, ChannelMembership, NotifyLevel, Message, MessageAction, FileMeta, ReactionGroup, Friendship, Invite, InviteStatus, AuditEntry, AuditAction, WorkspaceStatus, ServerInfo, BuildRevision, StorageUsage, SessionInfo, ThreadFollow, FollowedThread, ScheduledMessage, ScheduledStatus, App, ModalView, ModalField, Webhook, SlashCommand, EventSubscription, PROTOCOL_VERSION, SEND_RETRY_WINDOW_MS Used by: packages/protocol/src/events.ts, packages/protocol/src/huddle.ts, packages/protocol/src/index.ts, packages/protocol/src/permissions.ts, packages/server/test/purgedSendKeys.test.ts, scripts/measure-snapshot.mts ---- packages/protocol/src/rest.ts (312 lines, changed in 29 commits, added 2026-08-31, last changed 2026-10-01). It covers auth, profile, channels, messages, scheduling, search, history paging, invites, admin actions and every integration endpoint. Limits (lengths, counts, page sizes) live here so both sides share them. How it works: - Handles: 2-32 chars, lowercase letters, digits, . _ - - Messages: up to 12000 chars and 10 file ids; must have text or files (refine) - createChannelBody is a discriminated union over public/private/dm (exactly 1 member)/group_dm (2-8 members) - integrationUrl only accepts http(s) URLs without embedded credentials - Cursor for saved/pinned lists is 'timestamp:ULID' so ties on the same millisecond page deterministically - editMessageBody and editScheduledBody carry expectedText for edit-conflict detection; threadHistoryQuery allows only one of before/after/around Optimizations: - Page sizes are capped (e.g. history 200, search 100, saved 100) to bound query cost - Modal submission values are size-bounded before being echoed to apps Key exports: handleSchema, registerBody, loginBody, changePasswordBody, updateMeBody, channelPrefsBody, savedMessagesQuery, pinnedMessagesQuery, followedThreadsQuery, threadFollowBody, threadReadBody, markUnreadBody, createChannelBody, updateChannelBody, channelManagerBody, sendMessageBody, scheduleMessageBody, rescheduleBody, editScheduledBody, createAppBody, createWebhookBody, integrationUrl, createCommandBody, createSubscriptionBody, interactivityBody, messageActionBody, viewSubmitBody, adminUserBody, runCommandBody, editMessageBody, markReadBody, auditQuery, createInviteBody, messageHistoryQuery, searchQuery, activityQuery, threadHistoryQuery, RegisterBody and other z.infer types Used by: packages/protocol/src/index.ts, packages/ui/src/components/Composer.tsx

Protocol: the shared language · 3–4 of 9 smaller files

search.ts and events.ts

search.ts

Search query parser · 307 lines

Parses the search box syntax (from:, in:, has:, type:, before:, after:, plus free words) into a structured ParsedSearch shared by the server, which runs the query, and the client, which shows what it understood. Date modifiers are resolved to epoch-ms bounds in the reader's IANA time zone, correctly handling daylight-saving days. It also defines which MIME types and file extensions count as each attachment kind.

  • after: is exclusive of the named day, before: excludes the named day onwards, matching Slack

Optimization: Intl.DateTimeFormat instances are cached per canonical zone name in an LRU capped at 32, so arbitrary user-supplied zones cannot grow memory

events.ts

WebSocket event and message types · 185 lines

Defines everything that travels over the WebSocket. Durable WorkspaceEvents are appended to the event log with a monotonically increasing seq and replayed on reconnect; EphemeralEvents (typing, presence, read cursors, huddle signals, modals) are never stored. It also defines the ReadySnapshot sent after a hello and the full ServerToClient / ClientToServer message unions.

  • WorkspaceEvent covers message create/update/delete, reactions, pins, history.removed (retention), channel and member changes, and user join/update

Optimization: Reconnect replays only events after lastSeq instead of re-downloading state

Protocol: the shared language · 5–6 of 9 smaller files

discovery.ts and permissions.ts

discovery.ts

LAN discovery and deep links · 56 lines

Constants and helpers for finding a workspace on the local network and building join links. It names the mDNS service type and default port, describes the TXT record payload, and lists the deep-link schemes the app accepts (the current tandem:// plus two legacy names).

  • mDNS service type 'slackoss', default port 8543
  • TXT record: workspace name, server version, protocol version, optional per-start instance id
  • hostWithPort brackets IPv6 literals so a URL can separate host and port
  • isLinkableAddress rejects IPv6 link-local (fe80::/10) and zone-scoped addresses, which a browser URL cannot express

permissions.ts

Channel permission rules · 54 lines

Pure functions deciding who may manage a room, appoint managers, invite, or remove members. They are shared so the client can hide controls and the server can enforce the same rules.

  • Only public/private rooms can be managed; inactive users and bots get nothing
  • Owners/admins and the room creator (if still a member) can manage managers; delegated managers can manage
  • Visibility is checked separately: admins do not gain access to private rooms
  • Nobody can remove the owner or themselves; only the owner can remove an admin; only manageManagers can remove the creator or a manager

Protocol: the shared language · 7–8 of 9 smaller files

huddle.ts and format.ts

huddle.ts

Voice/video huddle signalling types · 51 lines

Types for the WebRTC handshake the server relays between huddle participants without touching media. It also defines the tie-break rule deciding which peer sends the offer.

  • HuddleSignal kinds: offer, answer, ice, and media (camera/screen/muted flags)
  • Uses plain objects rather than DOM types because the server has no lib.dom
  • The media signal exists because a remote track reports unmuted even when no frames arrive
  • shouldInitiateOffer: the lower user id offers, avoiding WebRTC glare

format.ts

Message text helpers · 41 lines

Small helpers for mrkdwn message text. escapeMrkdwn backslash-escapes formatting characters so text shows literally (motivated by /shrug), and broadcastsIn/broadcastLabel detect and display room-wide mentions such as <!channel> and <!here>.

  • Escapes backslash, *, _, ~ and backtick in a single regex pass
  • <!everyone> is accepted but treated as channel
  • broadcastLabel turns a token into @here / @channel

Area 2 of 14 · packages/server/src

Server source

This is the self-hosted workspace server: a Fastify HTTP server plus a WebSocket gateway on top of a single SQLite database (node:sqlite) and a folder of attachment blobs. main.ts is the CLI that parses flags and either runs a maintenance command (backup, restore, verify-backup, recover) or calls createWorkspaceServer in server.ts. server.ts takes an exclusive lock on the data directory (ownership.ts), opens and migrates the database (db.ts), wraps it in the Store data-access class (store.ts), and registers every REST route; each write runs inside mutate(), which commits rows plus an append-only event log in one transaction and only afterwards fans the events out through the Gateway (gateway.ts) to the sockets allowed to see them and queues them for subscribed apps. Clients reconnect with their last event seq and replay what they missed from that log. Supporting modules handle auth hashing, rate limiting, SSRF-safe outbound calls to apps, Slack-compatible payload translation, log redaction, security headers, storage accounting and backups.

Server · packages/server/src · part 1 of 3

server.ts

Server assembly, REST routes and background queues · 4,483 lines · changed in 95 commits

The core of the server. createWorkspaceServer locks the data directory, opens the database, builds the Store, Gateway, rate limiter and storage budget, registers all REST routes on Fastify (auth, users, channels, messages, files, reactions, pins, threads, scheduled messages, invites, search, admin, apps, webhooks, slash commands, Slack Web API methods, buttons and modals), and starts timers for the background queues. It returns a WorkspaceServer handle with control methods and a staged stop() for the CLI and the desktop app.

How it works

  • mutate(work) runs the write inside store.transaction, records events through recordEvent (append to the events table, stamp the message seq, auto-follow threads, queue app deliveries), then after commit runs side effects and publishCommitted fans the events out; a fan-out failure calls gateway.resynchronize() so clients replay from the log

Optimizations here

  • At most 2 scrypt password derivations at once (beginAuth); extra requests get 429 auth_busy
  • Each channel's audience is read once per committed change and shared across its events (audiences map, F10)
  • Mention counts are recomputed once per person per change, and only for people who are online

Server · packages/server/src · part 2 of 3

server.ts

Server assembly, REST routes and background queues · 4,483 lines · changed in 95 commits

How it works (continued)

  • postMessage is shared by the API and the scheduler: idempotent sends via (user, nonce) plus a request hash (409 nonce_conflict on mismatch), auto-joins public channels, checks thread roots and attachment ownership, and can mark a scheduled row sent in the same transaction
  • Bootstrap: generates workspace_id and a claim_code when there are no users; the first account must come from the local machine (isLocalRequest rejects forwarded headers and foreign Origins) or present the claim code
  • Uploads stream through a Transform that reserves storage per chunk, keeps the first 64 KB to read image dimensions, and writes with flag 'wx'; access is re-checked after streaming; on failure the blob is unlinked or queued for deletion
  • File downloads use either the bearer token or a 60-second single-use download ticket so browsers can stream to disk; session, file and channel access are re-checked after the async disk open
  • Outgoing app events: a durable event_deliveries queue drained by flushEventDeliveries, a pump with up to 10 in flight, one per subscription to keep order, a retry ladder, and abandonment of a dead endpoint's backlog; requests are HMAC-signed

More optimizations

  • Each event's app delivery body is built lazily once and bot channel membership is cached per event (F11)
  • Event delivery pump: up to 10 concurrent, one per subscription, at most 50 per round, nudged by new events
  • Scheduled messages, file deletions and retention work in batches or pages and yield to the event loop with setImmediate between them
  • Static web client served with preCompressed Brotli/gzip and year-long immutable caching for hashed assets
  • Uploads are streamed to disk instead of buffered; only the first 64 KB is kept for image sizing

Server · packages/server/src · part 1 of 3

store.ts

Data-access layer (SQLite repository) · 3,661 lines · changed in 60 commits

The Store class wraps the DatabaseSync connection and holds the SQL the server runs: users, sessions, channels, membership, messages, threads, files, reactions, pins, saved items, scheduled messages, apps, tokens, webhooks, slash commands, event subscriptions and their delivery queue, invites, audit log, the event log and search. It converts snake_case rows into protocol types and keeps rules such as visibility, unread state and mention indexing in one place.

How it works

  • transaction(work) runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT / ROLLBACK and is meant for synchronous work only; events are published after it returns
  • Event log: appendEvent writes the JSON payload with an autoincrement seq; eventsSince(afterSeq, user) returns the events the user may see (global, public, or channels they belong to), or null when the client is too far behind or there are more than 2000, which forces a fresh snapshot; pruneEvents keeps the newest 20,000

Optimizations here

  • Batched hydration: one query per related table for a whole page of messages instead of one per message
  • Denormalized message_mentions index (WITHOUT ROWID) for unread-mention badges

Server · packages/server/src · part 2 of 3

store.ts

Data-access layer (SQLite repository) · 3,661 lines · changed in 60 commits

How it works (continued)

  • Editing or deleting a message redacts earlier copies of its text, files and buttons in the event log and in queued app deliveries, keeping the seqs so replay still works
  • hydrateMessages loads reactions, reply counts, pins and files for a whole page of messages with one IN (...) query each
  • indexMentions keeps the message_mentions table ('!' means room-wide) so unreadMentionCounts reads only a user's mentions, not every message in their channels
  • purgeMessagesBefore removes whole threads past the retention cutoff under a message budget, using a temp table instead of bound parameters so a thread of any size fits
  • searchMessages: FTS5 MATCH with every term quoted, plus from:/in:/has:/before:/after:/type filters as SQL, attachment-name matching, and a visibility filter that always applies
  • Event delivery queue: at most 500 pending per subscription (extra events are counted as dropped), 1,000 failed kept for retry, and dueEventDeliveries returns only the oldest pending row per subscription so delivery stays in order

More optimizations

  • Search: counts FTS matches up to 5,001; when a term is that common it scans only the newest 20,000 messages (with a unary + so SQLite does not start from the FTS side), otherwise it starts from the matches (OPT-11, F13)
  • Backlog-full check uses LIMIT 1 OFFSET 499 instead of counting the whole queue
  • listChannelsVisibleTo loads every channel's managers and DM members in two grouped queries for the handshake (OPT-13)
  • Retention purges are bounded by a message budget and use a temp table to avoid parameter limits
  • Statements are prepared inline on each call; there is no prepared-statement cache

Server · packages/server/src · part 1 of 2

db.ts

SQLite schema, migrations and open · 811 lines · changed in 39 commits

Holds the ordered list of 37 SQL migrations that define the schema, and openDb, which opens the database with WAL, foreign keys and a busy timeout, then upgrades it to the latest version inside one transaction. Before an upgrade it takes a verified copy of the workspace with VACUUM INTO and keeps the three most recent copies.

How it works

  • The schema version is stored in PRAGMA user_version; SCHEMA_VERSION = MIGRATIONS.length; a database newer than the build is refused
  • v1 creates users, sessions, channels, channel_members, messages, reactions, invites, events, meta and an external-content FTS5 table messages_fts kept in sync by insert/delete/update triggers
  • Later migrations add files, pins, saved items, notification preferences, scheduled messages, apps, tokens, webhooks, slash commands, event subscriptions, friendships, buttons, send-key idempotency, session expiry, download tokens, the durable event_deliveries queue, audit_log, scheduled_files, message_mentions and purged_message_requests

Optimizations here

  • PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL and busy_timeout = 5000
  • Composite indexes for hot paths: messages(channel_id, id), messages(thread_root_id, id) (v28, measured 92 ms down to 3 ms), scheduled_messages(status, send_at), event_deliveries(failed_at, next_attempt_at, event_seq)

Server · packages/server/src · part 1 of 2

gateway.ts

WebSocket gateway and real-time fan-out · 723 lines · changed in 25 commits

The Gateway class owns every live WebSocket. It handles the hello handshake (token check, ready snapshot, replay of missed events), heartbeats, typing notices, presence and huddle (voice/video call) rooms with WebRTC signal relay, and sends durable and ephemeral events only to the sockets allowed to see them. It is attached to Fastify's HTTP server via the upgrade event at /ws.

How it works

  • Visibility: global events and public-channel events go to everyone; private and DM events go only to current members (audienceForChannel)
  • Handshake: checks the protocol version, resolves the session from the SHA-256 token hash, refuses accounts that must change their password, builds a ReadySnapshot (users, channels, memberships, last seqs, saved items, thread follows, mention counts, huddles, friends), then replays eventsSince(lastSeq) or sends resync; syncVersion 1 adds replayFrom and a synced marker
  • Unauthenticated sockets are closed after 10 s; a 30 s ping/pong heartbeat terminates dead connections

Optimizations here

  • Backpressure: a socket with more than 2 MB buffered is terminated rather than queued in memory
  • Each frame is JSON.stringify'd once per fan-out and sent as the same string to every recipient
  • byUser index means a fan-out reaches only the audience's sockets instead of scanning all of them (REV-06)

Server · packages/server/src · part 2 of 2

gateway.ts

WebSocket gateway and real-time fan-out · 723 lines · changed in 25 commits

How it works (continued)

  • Huddles are in-memory only (channelId to set of userIds); signals are relayed only between two participants of the same room who both still have access
  • Every socket callback runs inside contained() so a throw is reported and the socket closes with 1011 rather than crashing the process (F03)
  • Revocation: disconnectUser, disconnectSession and revoke close sockets with 4003; resynchronize/resynchronizeUser close with 1012 so clients replay from the log
  • Departures caused by failures are batched with setImmediate and announced together after one session check
  • Incoming frames are checked against the zod socketMessage schema; an invalid one closes the socket with 4000

More optimizations

  • sessionCheck caches each session's validity for the length of one fan-out
  • publish returns immediately when nobody is connected; audiences can be shared across one change's events
  • perMessageDeflate disabled and maxPayload capped at 128 KB
  • presenceMap lists only online users instead of every account (OPT-13)
  • Socket opens are rate-limited per address before the upgrade handshake; typing and signaling go through the ephemeral limit

Server · packages/server/src · part 1 of 2

main.ts

CLI entry point · 445 lines · changed in 20 commits

The command-line program (slackoss-server / Tandem server). It parses flags with node:util parseArgs, runs one of the maintenance subcommands (backup, verify-backup, restore, recover) or starts the server, then prints the local and LAN addresses and the claim code for an ownerless workspace. It turns bad settings and startup errors into plain messages instead of stack traces.

How it works

  • Flags include --data, --port, --host, --name, --invite-only, --no-mdns, --storage-limit-mb, --abandoned-upload-hours, --retention-days, --web, --public-url, --trust-proxy, --no-rate-limits, --skip-upgrade-backup, --isolated, --allow-private-hooks
  • Several settings also read env vars via envSetting (TANDEM_*, falling back to GATHERLINE_* and SLACKOSS_*)
  • verify-backup prints an inventory of what starting the backup would contact: app origins, waiting scheduled messages, undelivered app events, still-valid sessions

Optimizations here

No specific performance work in this file.

Server source · 1–2 of 23 smaller files

backup.ts and outbound.ts

backup.ts

Backup, verify and restore · 552 lines

Implements offline-safe backup and restore of a workspace directory. A backup is a VACUUM INTO snapshot of the database, copies of every attachment blob, and a manifest with SHA-256 checksums, row counts and schema version; a restore verifies and stages the backup next to the target, then swaps directories and keeps the old one.

  • backupWorkspace stages into a hidden .gatherline-backup-<uuid> operation directory with a journal record, holds a lock on it, verifies the copy, then renames it into place; leftover captures from crashed runs are cleaned up on the next run

Optimization: Checksums are computed by streaming files through createReadStream instead of reading them into memory

outbound.ts

SSRF-guarded outbound HTTP · 258 lines

postToUrl is the only way the server calls apps (slash commands, event subscriptions, interactivity). It blocks private, loopback, link-local and other reserved addresses unless --allow-private-hooks is set, and checks inside the socket's DNS lookup so DNS rebinding cannot get past it. Redirects are not followed, and both the response size and total time are capped.

  • IPv4 blocklist includes 0/8, 10/8, 127/8, 169.254/16 (cloud metadata), 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, 198.18/15 and 224+

Optimization: A hard total-time deadline in addition to the socket inactivity timeout, so a streaming endpoint cannot hold a call open

Server source · 3–4 of 23 smaller files

blockKit.ts and limits.ts

blockKit.ts

Slack Block Kit translation · 249 lines

Converts Slack Block Kit payloads from integrations into what Tandem can show: mrkdwn text from header, section, context and divider blocks, buttons from actions blocks, and modal forms from view objects. Unsupported elements are dropped instead of being rejected.

  • payloadToText uses text when it is present and falls back to the blocks, as Slack does
  • Buttons are limited to Slack's caps (25 actions, 75-character labels, 2000-character values) and only http(s) URLs are kept
  • parseView keeps only plain_text_input (text or textarea) and static_select fields and reports droppedFields; the caller can refuse a view whose fields were all dropped

limits.ts

Rate limits (token bucket) · 167 lines

Defines every rate limit the server applies and an in-memory token-bucket RateLimiter. Limits are keyed per account where there is one and per address otherwise, with burst and per-minute refill values chosen for office NAT and offline outbox flushes.

  • Limit names: authByHandle, authByAddress, post, upload, socket, ephemeral, hook, hookByAddress, appCall
  • take() spends nothing when it refuses, and returns retryAfterMs
  • forget() clears a handle's failed sign-in count after a correct password, so only wrong guesses count

Optimization: Full buckets are deleted, so the map grows only with currently active callers

Server source · 5–6 of 23 smaller files

integrations.ts and ownership.ts

integrations.ts

Slack-compatible event mapping and signing · 153 lines

Helpers for outgoing integrations. It signs request bodies the way Slack does (HMAC-SHA256 over v0:timestamp:body) and sends both Slack and SlackOSS header names; it converts internal WorkspaceEvents into Slack Events API payloads; and it finds who caused an event so a bot is never sent its own actions.

  • Message ids are used as Slack's ts, since ULIDs sort in time order like Slack timestamps
  • Maps message created/changed/deleted, reactions, pins, member join/leave, channel created/renamed and team_join/user_change
  • Events with no Slack equivalent return null and are not delivered

ownership.ts

Exclusive workspace lock · 144 lines

Makes sure only one process (server, restore, recovery) writes a data directory at a time. It opens a small workspace.lock SQLite database and holds an uncommitted BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, so the operating system releases the lock if the process dies, and it writes a workspace.owner.json describing the holder for error messages.

  • busy_timeout 0 and journal_mode DELETE so the lock lives on the file itself, not in WAL shared memory
  • A second holder gets WorkspaceInUseError naming the purpose, pid, host, port and start time from the owner file
  • The owner file is written atomically (write to a temp file, then rename); describe() adds the port once listening

Server source · 7–8 of 23 smaller files

recover.ts and netTrust.ts

recover.ts

Offline account recovery · 128 lines

Backs the CLI's recover command, which runs against the database file while the server is stopped. It can list human accounts, or issue a temporary password for one account, reactivate it, optionally make it owner, end its sessions and write an audit record, all in one transaction.

  • Takes the workspace lock first, so it refuses to run while a server is running
  • The temporary password is 16 hex characters with must_change_password set, so it cannot become a lasting password
  • --make-owner demotes any existing owner to admin, the same as a normal ownership transfer

netTrust.ts

Client address and origin trust · 116 lines

Pure functions that decide how far to trust request metadata. They compute the server's origin from the socket, check whether an Origin header is this same server on loopback, and resolve the client IP used for rate limits, trusting forwarded headers only from a loopback proxy such as the desktop app's cloudflared connector.

  • By default only the socket peer address is used
  • In loopback-proxy mode it prefers a single cf-connecting-ip value, then the rightmost X-Forwarded-For hop, so a client-supplied earlier entry cannot pick its own rate-limit bucket

Server source · 9–10 of 23 smaller files

redact.ts and config.ts

redact.ts

Log redaction · 107 lines

Keeps credentials out of request logs. redactUrl masks secret path segments (invite codes, webhook tokens, response URLs) and credential-like query parameters, and LOGGER_OPTIONS configures Pino to remove auth headers and use the redacted URL.

  • Secret path prefixes: /api/invites/, /hooks/, /api/commands/response/
  • Query parameters download, token, ticket, code and secret are matched case-insensitively by whole name
  • A query name that cannot be decoded is masked entirely instead of throwing
  • Removes the authorization, cookie, x-slackoss-signature and set-cookie headers

config.ts

Settings validation · 101 lines

Checks operator-supplied settings before the server uses them and produces clear ConfigError messages that name the flag. It also turns common startup failures (port in use, permission denied, bad host) into plain advice.

  • envSetting reads TANDEM_*, then GATHERLINE_*, then SLACKOSS_* so older deployments keep working
  • parsePublicUrl requires http(s), refuses credentials, query strings and fragments (the URL is given to every app), and strips trailing slashes
  • describeStartupError maps EADDRINUSE, EACCES, ENOTFOUND and EADDRNOTAVAIL to explanations

How it works: - Secret path prefixes: /api/invites/, /hooks/, /api/commands/response/ - Query parameters download, token, ticket, code and secret are matched case-insensitively by whole name - A query name that cannot be decoded is masked entirely instead of throwing - Removes the authorization, cookie, x-slackoss-signature and set-cookie headers Key exports: redactUrl, LOGGER_OPTIONS Used by: packages/server/src/server.ts, packages/server/test/redact.test.ts ---- packages/server/src/config.ts (101 lines, changed in 3 commits, added 2026-09-13, last changed 2026-10-02). Checks operator-supplied settings before the server uses them and produces clear ConfigError messages that name the flag. It also turns common startup failures (port in use, permission denied, bad host) into plain advice. How it works: - envSetting reads TANDEM_*, then GATHERLINE_*, then SLACKOSS_* so older deployments keep working - parsePublicUrl requires http(s), refuses credentials, query strings and fragments (the URL is given to every app), and strips trailing slashes - describeStartupError maps EADDRINUSE, EACCES, ENOTFOUND and EADDRNOTAVAIL to explanations Key exports: ConfigError, envSetting, parsePort, parsePublicUrl, parseWholeNumber, describeStartupError Used by: packages/server/src/main.ts, packages/server/src/server.ts, packages/server/test/config.test.ts

Server source · 11–12 of 23 smaller files

securityHeaders.ts and imageSize.ts

securityHeaders.ts

CSP and security headers · 63 lines

Defines the Content-Security-Policy and other security headers that server.ts adds to every response. script-src 'self' stops injected markup from running as code, while connect-src stays open so the browser client can connect to any workspace.

  • Directives include frame-ancestors 'none', object-src 'none', and img-src/media-src allowing blob: for previews
  • The META variant leaves out frame-ancestors, which a meta tag cannot set (used by the desktop app)
  • Also sets referrer-policy no-referrer (tokens appear in some URLs), x-content-type-options nosniff and x-frame-options DENY

imageSize.ts

Image dimension sniffing · 62 lines

Reads width and height directly from PNG, GIF, WebP (VP8, VP8L, VP8X) and JPEG headers without a native decoder. The server stores these with each upload so clients can reserve space before the image loads.

  • JPEG walks marker segments to the first SOFn frame header, skipping SOF4, SOF8 and SOF12
  • Returns null for unrecognized or too-short buffers

Optimization: Works on only the first 64 KB of an upload, so the image is never decoded or fully buffered

Server source · 13–14 of 23 smaller files

storageBudget.ts and capabilities.ts

storageBudget.ts

Attachment storage quota · 51 lines

Tracks bytes used by attachment blobs and enforces the optional storage cap while several uploads stream at once. It scans the files directory at startup and then reserves space chunk by chunk as uploads arrive.

  • reserve(id, bytes) fails when the chunk would exceed the limit; a null limit means unlimited
  • Reserving per chunk means two uploads that reach the limit together can both be refused; this is accepted so the limit is never exceeded
  • storedIds() lists counted blobs so the server can find blobs on disk with no database row

Optimization: Usage is counted in memory, so the directory is not re-scanned for each upload

capabilities.ts

Bounded expiring capability map · 50 lines

CapabilityMap stores short-lived tokens given to apps (response_url, trigger_id, open modal views) with a fixed ceiling. Because every entry in one map has the same lifetime, insertion order is expiry order, so expired entries are swept from the front and the oldest is evicted when the map is over its ceiling.

  • get() treats an expired entry as missing and deletes it
  • set() re-inserts the key to move it to the end, then evicts from the front past the ceiling

Optimization: The sweep stops at the first entry that has not expired instead of scanning the whole map, relying on JS Map insertion order

Server source · 15–16 of 23 smaller files

commands.ts and socketSchema.ts

commands.ts

Built-in slash commands · 43 lines

Defines the slash commands the server handles itself, /shrug and /me, so a workspace with no apps still has them and apps cannot claim those names.

  • /shrug appends the shrug art, pre-escaped with escapeMrkdwn so the backslash survives rendering
  • /me wraps the text in underscores (italics); it returns null for empty text to signal a usage error

socketSchema.ts

WebSocket message validation · 37 lines

A zod discriminated union describing every frame a client may send over the socket: hello, ping, typing, huddle.join, huddle.leave and huddle.signal. The gateway rejects anything that does not match.

  • hello carries token, lastSeq, protocolVersion and an optional syncVersion of 1
  • WebRTC signals are offer, answer, ice or media, with size limits on SDP (100 KB) and ICE candidates
  • IDs are 1 to 128 characters long

Server source · 17–18 of 23 smaller files

auth.ts and ids.ts

auth.ts

Password and token hashing · 33 lines

Small crypto helpers. Passwords are hashed with scrypt and a random 16-byte salt and checked with a constant-time comparison; session tokens are 32 random bytes, and only their SHA-256 hash is stored.

  • scrypt with a 64-byte key, run through the async callback API so it stays off the main thread
  • verifyPassword checks the lengths match before timingSafeEqual
  • hashToken (SHA-256 hex) is also used for download tickets, webhook tokens and send-request hashes

Optimization: Async scrypt runs on the libuv thread pool so it does not block the event loop

ids.ts

ID and secret generation · 30 lines

Generates identifiers. ulid() produces a 26-character Crockford base32 id (10 timestamp characters plus 16 random) that sorts by time; inviteCode() makes 8-character codes, and secretToken() makes 48-hex-character secrets for bot tokens and webhooks.

  • Because ULIDs sort by time, message ids work as pagination cursors (ORDER BY id) and as Slack ts values
  • All randomness comes from crypto.randomBytes

Optimization: Time-sortable ids let the messages(channel_id, id) index serve both lookup and chronological paging

Server source · 19–20 of 23 smaller files

mdns.ts and webClient.ts

mdns.ts

LAN discovery advertisement · 30 lines

Advertises the workspace on the local network with Bonjour/mDNS so clients can list it on their Join screen. The TXT record carries the workspace name, server version, protocol version and instance id.

  • Uses MDNS_SERVICE_TYPE from the protocol package
  • server.ts re-advertises when the workspace is renamed and skips advertising in --isolated mode

webClient.ts

Web client caching rules · 28 lines

Decides the Cache-Control header for files of the bundled browser client and which unmatched requests should get a 404 instead of the SPA's index.html.

  • Files under assets/ have content-hashed names and get public, max-age=31536000, immutable
  • Everything else, including index.html, gets no-cache so the browser revalidates (304 when unchanged)
  • A missing /assets/ file returns 404 so an old chunk is not answered with HTML

Optimization: Year-long immutable caching for hashed build assets with revalidation for the HTML entry (REV-13)

ICE server config · 26 lines

Validates the STUN/TURN server list used for huddle calls, supplied as JSON in TANDEM_ICE_SERVERS, and fails with a clear message when it is malformed.

Holds SERVER_VERSION and, when built, the source revision stamped in by the build. It is a separate file so the backup and mDNS code can name the version without loading the whole HTTP server.

Area 3 of 14 · packages/server/test

Server tests

The server's vitest suite, about 65 files. Most tests start a real server with createWorkspaceServer on port 0 (dataDir ':memory:' or a mkdtemp folder when files or restarts matter) and talk to it with real fetch calls and ws WebSockets; some spawn child processes or stub app HTTP servers. Store-level tests open the SQLite database directly with openDb/openDbAtVersion, and several inject failures with vi.spyOn on the store or gateway. Categories: core end-to-end behaviour, auth and security, integrations and Slack compatibility, reliability under failure, backup/restore and upgrades, retention and privacy, and performance checks (call counting and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN).

It protects integrity checks (inventory, checksums, schema) and that restoring preserves data and never damages the current workspace. packages/server/test/backupImports.test.ts: Scans the import graph of the backup module to make sure a backup job loads only what it needs (REV-07). Loading Fastify, sockets and mDNS cost a backup worker about half its startup time and memory. packages/server/test/backupPublication.test.ts: Checks that a backup destination only becomes visible once its contents are copied and verified, and that interrupted or failed attempts are cleaned up and retryable. packages/server/test/capabilities.test.ts: Unit-tests CapabilityMap, the store for short-lived capabilities handed to apps (INT-01). It protects expiry and the ceiling on live entries. packages/server/test/channelManagers.test.ts: Exercises who may manage public and private rooms over HTTP for every kind of person. It holds the server routes to the shared permission functions in the protocol package.

Area 4 of 14 · packages/client-core

Client core

client-core is the framework-agnostic client engine shared by the desktop and web apps: it holds no UI, only connection logic, state and rules. WorkspaceClient (workspace.ts) owns a typed REST client (api.ts), a self-reconnecting WebSocket, an authenticated blob cache (fileCache.ts) and a Zustand vanilla store; the server's 'ready' snapshot and numbered events flow over the socket into that store, REST calls page history and perform actions, and the UI subscribes to the store to render. Around it sit smaller pure modules: notification rules (notify.ts), WebRTC huddles (huddle.ts) with user-facing capture errors (capture.ts), and plain-data merge functions for outbox, drafts and records that let several windows on one device share stored state safely. index.ts re-exports the public surface, and the tests mix pure unit tests with integration tests against a real in-memory workspace server.

Client core · packages/client-core/src · part 1 of 5

workspace.ts

Live workspace client and state store · 3,099 lines · changed in 51 commits

WorkspaceClient is the heart of the client: one instance per connected workspace server, combining the typed REST Api, a self-reconnecting WebSocket, a FileCache and a Zustand vanilla store (WorkspaceState) that is the local replica the UI renders from. Server snapshots and numbered events are folded into the store, history is paged in bounded windows, sends are optimistic with a nonce-keyed outbox, and read cursors, pins, saves, snooze, notification prefs and huddles are all managed here.

How it works

  • State model: WorkspaceState holds users, channels, memberships (channelId -> lastReadSeq), repliesRead, prefs/prefsWrites, channelLastSeq, presence, typing expiries, lastSeq, timelines (per-channel ChannelTimeline), threads + threadPages, pending sends, saved ids, threadFollows, mentionCounts, drafts, huddles, ephemerals, modal, commands and the current huddle.

Optimizations here

  • Timeline capped at 300 messages (MAX_TIMELINE_ITEMS) and threads at 300 replies (THREAD_WINDOW); the trimmed end is re-fetchable on scroll.
  • Only 20 timelines and 20 threads kept in memory (HISTORY_CACHE_LIMIT), evicted least-recently-used; the visible conversation and thread are protected.

WorkspaceClient is the heart of the client: one instance per connected workspace server, combining the typed REST Api, a self-reconnecting WebSocket, a FileCache and a Zustand vanilla store (WorkspaceState) that is the local replica the UI renders from. Server snapshots and numbered events are folded into the store, history is paged in bounded windows, sends are optimistic with a nonce-keyed outbox, and read cursors, pins, saves, snooze, notification prefs and huddles are all managed here. How it works: - State model: WorkspaceState holds users, channels, memberships (channelId -> lastReadSeq), repliesRead, prefs/prefsWrites, channelLastSeq, presence, typing expiries, lastSeq, timelines (per-channel ChannelTimeline), threads + threadPages, pending sends, saved ids, threadFollows, mentionCounts, drafts, huddles, ephemerals, modal, commands and the current huddle. - Connection: connect() opens ws(s)://.../ws and sends a 'hello' with token, lastSeq and PROTOCOL_VERSION. On close it reconnects with exponential backoff (1s doubling to 30s), but stops for good on close codes 4003 (auth_failed), 4002 (protocol_mismatch) and 4004 (password_change_required). - applyReady() rebuilds users/channels/memberships/prefs from the 'ready' snapshot, drops channels no longer visible, keeps loaded timelines/threads/pending/drafts so replayed events patch them, and resets history when the server has no replay (replayFrom null) or has gone backwards. It refuses (destroys and sets auth_failed) if the snapshot is for a different user or workspace id. - applyEvent() ignores events at or below lastSeq, skips replayed channel/member/user events already reflected in the snapshot, and handles message.created/updated/deleted, history.removed (retention), reactions, pins, channel and member changes and user updates. An HTTP send result is applied immediately and remembered so its later socket echo is not applied twice. - applyEphemeral() handles non-sequenced pushes: presence, typing (5s expiry, swept every 2s), channel.access grants/revocations, channel.read/unread, prefs, saved, mentions, thread.follow, huddle participants/signals/join results, slash-command ephemeral answers and app modal views. - History paging: loadTimeline (tail or older, 50 per page), jumpToMessage (window around a message), loadNewer (forward from an anchored view) and loadThread (latest/older/newer/around). Each request records socket events that arrive while it is in flight (up to 2000) and replays only those newer than the response's snapshot seq via per-message watermarks (snapshotSeq/messageSnapshots), so nothing is lost or applied twice. - Timelines are capped at 300 items and threads at 300 replies; trimming one end marks it pageable again (hasMore/hasMoreNewer). An anchored view (hasMoreNewer) does not get live messages appended, to avoid faking adjacency across a gap. - Unread logic: isMessageRead() is the shared rule. Top-level messages read by the channel cursor; replies by the thread's cursor or the membership's repliesRead; broadcast replies by either, unless a thread unreadHold applies. markRead updates optimistically and queues pendingReads, flushed on sync and every 5s; markUnread/markThreadUnread set holds so automatic acknowledgement cannot immediately re-read them. - Sending: send() creates a random 16-byte hex nonce, shows a PendingMessage at once (with image object-URL previews), uploads files with progress, then POSTs the message. Failures are classified as refusals (4xx except 401/408/429) or retryable, with human-readable reasons. Leading '/word' text runs a slash command instead. OUTBOX_LIMIT caps waiting sends at 50. - Outbox persistence: outboxSnapshot()/restoreOutbox() let the app store pending sends across restarts. Client core · packages/client-core/src · part 2 of 5

workspace.ts

Live workspace client and state store · 3,099 lines · changed in 51 commits

How it works (continued)

  • Connection: connect() opens ws(s)://.../ws and sends a 'hello' with token, lastSeq and PROTOCOL_VERSION. On close it reconnects with exponential backoff (1s doubling to 30s), but stops for good on close codes 4003 (auth_failed), 4002 (protocol_mismatch) and 4004 (password_change_required).
  • applyReady() rebuilds users/channels/memberships/prefs from the 'ready' snapshot, drops channels no longer visible, keeps loaded timelines/threads/pending/drafts so replayed events patch them, and resets history when the server has no replay (replayFrom null) or has gone backwards. It refuses (destroys and sets auth_failed) if the snapshot is for a different user or workspace id.
  • applyEvent() ignores events at or below lastSeq, skips replayed channel/member/user events already reflected in the snapshot, and handles message.created/updated/deleted, history.removed (retention), reactions, pins, channel and member changes and user updates. An HTTP send result is applied immediately and remembered so its later socket echo is not applied twice.
  • applyEphemeral() handles non-sequenced pushes: presence, typing (5s expiry, swept every 2s), channel.access grants/revocations, channel.read/unread, prefs, saved, mentions, thread.follow, huddle participants/signals/join results, slash-command ephemeral answers and app modal views.

More optimizations

  • Identical in-flight history requests are shared (same key returns the same promise); a superseded request is aborted with AbortController.
  • Events buffered during a history load are capped at 2000 (HISTORY_EVENTS_LIMIT); overflow fails the load with history_changed instead of risking wrong state.
  • sortedInsert fast-paths appending in-order messages instead of sorting.
  • Thread updates skip setting state for threads an event does not touch, so unrelated views do not re-render (REV-03).
  • WebSocket reconnect uses exponential backoff from 1s up to 30s, reset on ready.

workspace.ts

Live workspace client and state store · 3,099 lines · changed in 51 commits

How it works (continued)

  • Sending: send() creates a random 16-byte hex nonce, shows a PendingMessage at once (with image object-URL previews), uploads files with progress, then POSTs the message. Restored sends are re-delivered with the same nonce unless they had attachments (files are not kept), were refused, or are older than SEND_RETRY_WINDOW_MS; adoptRefusal() takes on another window's refusal.
  • Optimistic choices: pins, saves and Do Not Disturb go through choose()/sendChoice(), which keeps one request in flight per key, shows the latest choice, sends the newest waiting choice next, and resends once if the server reported a different value meanwhile. Notification prefs use a similar per-channel confirmed/inFlight/queued/failed queue; thread follows use revision numbers so stale echoes cannot undo newer state.

Client core · packages/client-core/src · part 1 of 2

api.ts

Typed REST client · 722 lines · changed in 51 commits

Api is a thin typed wrapper over fetch for every REST endpoint of one workspace server: auth, sessions, users, channels, messages and history pages, threads, reactions, pins, saves, files, scheduled messages, apps/webhooks/commands, admin, invites, activity and search. Errors become ApiError carrying the HTTP status and server error code. normalizeServerUrl turns whatever a user typed into a server origin.

How it works

  • Private request() adds a Bearer token and JSON content type, supports per-call timeouts via AbortSignal.timeout combined with a caller signal using AbortSignal.any, and parses {error, message} from failed responses.
  • uploadFile uses XMLHttpRequest (not fetch) so it can report upload progress; 5-minute timeout, abortable via signal, and maps failures to ApiError codes like network_error, aborted, upload_timeout.
  • fetchFile downloads raw bytes with the token and cache: 'no-store' (to bypass bytes older servers marked immutable), with a 5-minute timeout.

Optimizations here

  • Per-request timeouts (typically 4-20s; 5 min for file transfers) so stalled calls fail instead of hanging.
  • Request cancellation via AbortSignal, merged with timeouts using AbortSignal.any.
  • Paged list endpoints (pins, saved, followed threads, activity, search, audit) use cursors with limit 30.

Client core · packages/client-core/src · part 1 of 2

huddle.ts

WebRTC huddle (voice/video call) session · 717 lines · changed in 11 commits

HuddleSession runs a full-mesh WebRTC call for one channel: one RTCPeerConnection per other participant, each with three fixed media slots (microphone, camera, screen). It handles offer/answer/ICE signalling through a transport supplied by WorkspaceClient, camera and screen toggles, mute, speaking indicators and microphone recovery. testMicrophone lets someone check their mic level before a call.

How it works

  • Only one side offers, decided by shouldInitiateOffer(selfId, peerId) from protocol, so offers never collide; the offerer creates the audio, camera and screen transceivers in that order and the answerer adopts them from the offer.
  • Camera and screen start/stop use replaceTrack on the existing transceivers, so no renegotiation is needed; a 'media' signal tells peers what is being sent and whether the mic is muted.
  • ICE candidates that arrive before the remote description are buffered (max 128 per peer) and flushed after it is set.

Optimizations here

  • Speaking detection reads the browser's already-parsed RTP audio level instead of a Web Audio graph per peer, to save CPU in larger calls.
  • Level polling publishes to the UI only when someone's speaking state actually changes, avoiding re-renders 8 times a second.
  • Media slots are fixed up front so camera/screen changes need no SDP renegotiation.

Client core · packages/client-core/src · part 2 of 2

huddle.ts

WebRTC huddle (voice/video call) session · 717 lines · changed in 11 commits

How it works (continued)

  • syncParticipants() reconciles the mesh with the room roster: dials new people, closes connections to those who left.
  • Speaking indicators: remote levels read from RTP synchronization sources, local level from an AnalyserNode; polled every 120ms with a 500ms hold to avoid flicker, and onChange fires only on a real transition.
  • Microphone recovery: when the mic track ends (unplugged or permission revoked) it asks for a new default mic, replaces it on every peer keeping the mute state, or sets micLost, tells peers it is muted and waits for a devicechange event.
  • Capture constraints: camera ideal 960x540 at 24fps (max 1280x720/30); screen max 1920x1080 at 15fps with contentHint 'detail' to keep text sharp.
  • destroy() stops every track, closes all peer connections, the AudioContext and timers, and stops listening for devices.

More optimizations

  • Early ICE candidates buffered with a 128 cap.
  • Concurrent camera/screen permission requests are deduplicated (acquiringCamera/acquiringScreen); concurrent mic recoveries share one promise.
  • Screen share capped at 1080p/15fps because each viewer is encoded separately in a mesh.

Client core · 1–2 of 7 smaller files

fileCache.ts and outbox.ts

fileCache.ts

Authenticated attachment cache · 234 lines

Because uploads require the session token, an <img src> cannot load them directly. FileCache fetches each file once with the token, turns it into a blob: URL, and shares it between views. It limits concurrent downloads, keeps idle files within a byte budget, and drops a file's bytes when its message is deleted, its conversation becomes unreadable, retention removes it, or the session ends.

  • get(fileId) returns a cached blob URL (refreshing its LRU position), joins an in-flight download, or queues a new one.

Optimization: Concurrent requests for the same file are deduplicated into one download.

outbox.ts

Cross-window outbox merge · 216 lines

Pure-data functions for storing unsent messages on the device when several windows share one account. Each window writes only its own puts and removals; the merge keeps tombstones so a delivered or discarded send can never be resurrected by a stale window, and the newer revision of a send wins. Kept free of side effects so the desktop main process can run the same merge.

  • Stored shape is {outbox: 2, entries, removed, compactedThrough?}; readStoredOutbox also accepts the older plain-array format, treating its entries as revision 0.

Optimization: Tombstones compacted to a single compactedThrough floor past 500 (or the retry window), hard-capped at 10,000 (about 660 KiB) to bound storage and merge time.

packages/client-core/src/fileCache.ts (234 lines, changed in 9 commits, added 2026-08-31, last changed 2026-10-04). Because uploads require the session token, an <img src> cannot load them directly. FileCache fetches each file once with the token, turns it into a blob: URL, and shares it between views. It limits concurrent downloads, keeps idle files within a byte budget, and drops a file's bytes when its message is deleted, its conversation becomes unreadable, retention removes it, or the session ends. How it works: - get(fileId) returns a cached blob URL (refreshing its LRU position), joins an in-flight download, or queues a new one. - retain/release count active views; releasing the last view cancels an unfinished download and lets the file become idle. - At most 4 transfers run at once; the rest wait in a queue and a slot is held for the full body transfer. - Idle (unretained) files are evicted oldest-first once their total exceeds maxIdleBytes (32 MiB default), revoking their object URLs. - Each file remembers its owner message/channel/thread root (asked from WorkspaceClient at fetch time) so invalidateMessage, invalidateChannel, invalidateRoots and invalidateAll can remove the right bytes even after the history that listed them was evicted (F07). - invalidate() aborts any transfer, revokes the URL, and notifies onInvalidate listeners so previews can show the file is gone; a late download result for an invalidated file is discarded. - dispose() aborts everything and clears all maps. Optimizations: - Concurrent requests for the same file are deduplicated into one download. - Download concurrency capped at 4. - LRU eviction of idle blobs within a 32 MiB budget; retained (visible) files are never evicted. - Unneeded downloads are aborted when the last view releases a file. - peek() returns an already-resolved URL synchronously for a first paint with no flash. Key exports: FileCache, FileOwner Imports: packages/protocol/src/index.ts, packages/client-core/src/api.ts Used by: packages/client-core/src/index.ts, packages/client-core/src/workspace.ts, packages/client-core/test/fileCache.test.ts, packages/client-core/test/fileInvalidation.test.ts ---- packages/client-core/src/outbox.ts (216 lines, changed in 2 commits, added 2026-09-30, last changed 2026-09-30). Pure-data functions for storing unsent messages on the device when several windows share one account. Each window writes only its own puts and removals; the merge keeps tombstones so a delivered or discarded send can never be resurrected by a stale window, and the newer revision of a send wins. Kept free of side effects so the desktop main process can run the same merge. How it works: - Stored shape is {outbox: 2, entries, removed, compactedThrough?}; readStoredOutbox also accepts the older plain-array format, treating its entries as revision 0. - outboxRevision returns max(previous + 1, now * 1000): wall-clock milliseconds with room for a counter, so revisions increase across windows. - mergeOutbox: removals become tombstones (final); a put is ignored if tombstoned, if an equal or newer revision is held, or if it is at or below the compaction floor. - Tombstones are kept newest-first: every one inside SEND_RETRY_WINDOW_MS, never fewer than 500 and never more than 10,000; the newest one let go raises compactedThrough, which never goes down. - storedPending normalizes an entry to a fixed shape so copies compare by JSON and extra fields are dropped. - applyOutboxChanges does the whole atomic step: unwrap (optionally a {version:1, value} envelope), merge, re-wrap; unreadable stored values are replaced instead of blocking later saves. Optimizations: - Tombstones compacted to a single compactedThrough floor past 500 (or the retry window), hard-capped at 10,000 (about 660 KiB) to bound storage and merge time. - Per-change merges instead of whole-list writes avoid lost updates between windows. drafts.ts

Cross-window draft merge · 127 lines

Pure-data helpers for storing composer drafts (one text per conversation key) shared by every window on one account. Windows send only the drafts they put or removed; if another window changed the same draft since this one last saw it, both texts are kept instead of one silently overwriting the other.

  • DraftChanges has put, remove, optional fill (only written where no draft exists, for migrating an older version's drafts) and optional base (what this window last knew for each key).

Optimization: Writes only changed keys rather than the whole draft set, avoiding cross-window lost updates.

notify.ts

Desktop notification rules · 126 lines

Decides whether an incoming message should raise a desktop notification, whether it is already on screen, and what text the notification shows. Lives here rather than in the UI so the rules are testable and identical on every client.

  • decideNotification checks in order: own message, not a member, muted, level 'nothing', mentions-only without being addressed (DMs always count), Do Not Disturb, then returns dm / mention / broadcast / all.
  • Room-wide mentions (@channel/@here/@everyone via broadcastsIn) count only outside DMs; @here rings only for live messages, not ones replayed after a reconnect.
