packages/client-core/src/drafts.ts (127 lines, changed in 2 commits, added 2026-09-30, last changed 2026-10-02). Pure-data helpers for storing composer drafts (one text per conversation key) shared by every window on one account. Windows send only the drafts they put or removed; if another window changed the same draft since this one last saw it, both texts are kept instead of one silently overwriting the other. How it works: - DraftChanges has put, remove, optional fill (only written where no draft exists, for migrating an older version's drafts) and optional base (what this window last knew for each key). - Conflict detection: a key is 'changed elsewhere' if base is given and the stored text differs from it; then a put keeps both texts and a removal leaves the other window's text in place. - keepBothDrafts returns the text that already contains the other, or both joined by a blank line, this window's first. - isDraftChanges validates the shape of incoming changes (strings only, base values string or null). - applyDraftChanges performs the full atomic update, supporting an optional {version: 1, value} envelope; unreadable stored values are replaced. Optimizations: - Writes only changed keys rather than the whole draft set, avoiding cross-window lost updates. Client core · 5–6 of 7 smaller files

capture.ts and records.ts

capture.ts

Media capture error wording · 65 lines

Turns a browser error from getUserMedia/getDisplayMedia into a sentence a person can act on, for microphone, camera or screen share. Returns null when nothing needs saying, such as the person simply closing the screen picker.

  • Decides by the DOMException name: NotSupportedError, NotAllowedError/SecurityError, NotFoundError/OverconstrainedError, NotReadableError/AbortError, else a generic retry message.
  • On an insecure (non-HTTPS) page, NotSupportedError says the desktop app or HTTPS is needed.
  • A closed screen picker returns null, but a refusal whose message mentions 'system' points to OS privacy settings.

records.ts

Cross-window key/value merge · 65 lines

A small plain-data record of text values by name (for example per-account notification choices) shared across windows on one device. Each window writes only the names it changed, so one window's choice cannot erase another's.

  • RecordChanges maps a name to a string, or null to remove it.
  • isRecordChanges accepts at most 64 names, each name and value at most 1024 characters.
  • readStoredRecord returns {} for nothing, null for anything that is not a record of strings.

Optimization: Input bounded to 64 names and 1024 characters per name/value.

Area 5 of 14 · packages/ui/src

UI shell, screens and helpers

The shell (apps/web or apps/desktop) renders <App platform={...}/>; App reads saved sign-ins from platform storage, then shows the lazy-loaded JoinScreen for picking a workspace and signing in, or WorkspaceScreen with a live WorkspaceClient for the chat itself. Everything shell-specific goes through the Platform interface in platform.ts: the desktop app supplies hosting, LAN discovery and its own storage, while webPlatform() implements storage on deviceStore, which keeps data in IndexedDB with a synchronous localStorage journal and cross-tab BroadcastChannel notices (falling back to localStorage only where IndexedDB is unavailable). Per-workspace data such as drafts, outbox, recent searches and the last conversation is stored under account-scoped keys built by lib/workspaceStorage.ts; device-wide preferences (appearance, composer, calls, notification previews) are small zustand stores cached per Platform. The rest of lib/ is pure helpers and React hooks for routing, deep links, formatting, accessibility (tabs, listbox, roving focus, panel focus) and support diagnostics, used by the screens and components.

UI · packages/ui/src/screens · part 1 of 2

WorkspaceScreen.tsx

Main workspace screen · 1,205 lines · changed in 64 commits

The signed-in workspace view: sidebar, conversation timeline, composer, side panels (thread, pins, saved, threads, scheduled, activity, members) and dialogs. It keeps the URL/history in sync with what is open, handles global keyboard shortcuts, and drives desktop notifications and reconnect catch-up summaries.

How it works

  • WorkspaceScreen provides ClientContext and wraps the inner screen in WorkspaceStorageGate and ShareableServerProvider; on desktop it adds a drag-region title bar.
  • Initial place comes from a deep-link target, else currentRoute (history state or #/c/... hash), else the last conversation saved for this account, else #general.
  • Only one side panel (SidePanel union) and one dialog (DialogKind union) are open at a time; panels, settings dialogs and the phone drawer are written into history via writeRoute so Back closes them.

Optimizations here

  • Rarely used panels and dialogs (Activity, Scheduled, Search, Account, People, Apps, Friends, Profile, Diagnostics, Channel details, new-channel forms, HuddleStage) are React.lazy-loaded to keep the initial download under about half a megabyte.
  • openMessage is a stable callback backed by a ref, so message links do not force every message to re-render.

packages/ui/src/screens/WorkspaceScreen.tsx (1,205 lines, changed in 64 commits, added 2026-08-31, last changed 2026-10-04). The signed-in workspace view: sidebar, conversation timeline, composer, side panels (thread, pins, saved, threads, scheduled, activity, members) and dialogs. It keeps the URL/history in sync with what is open, handles global keyboard shortcuts, and drives desktop notifications and reconnect catch-up summaries. UI · packages/ui/src/screens · part 2 of 2

WorkspaceScreen.tsx

Main workspace screen · 1,205 lines · changed in 64 commits

How it works (continued)

  • Global shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd+K quick switcher, Ctrl/Cmd+F search, Ctrl/Cmd+/ shortcuts, Escape closes the drawer or side panel; ignored while a modal is open or during IME composition.
  • jumpToMessage asks the client to load history around a message, then opens its channel (and thread if it is a reply), guarded by a navigation ticket.
  • client.onIncomingMessage decides notifications with client-core's decideNotification and isMessageOnScreen, respects the per-account notification preview setting, and tags notifications per account.
  • Messages caught up during a reconnect go into a CatchUpSummary and are shown as one summary notification instead of many.
  • When the connection status becomes auth_failed or password_change_required it calls onSignedOut.

More optimizations

  • Notification and catch-up handlers are installed in useLayoutEffect so a message arriving right after a conversation change is judged against the right screen state.
  • Notification preview choice and 'what is covered' are read from refs at message time, avoiding handler reinstallation.
  • The chat stays mounted (inert) under an expanded huddle video, so it keeps its scroll position.
  • Navigation tickets discard stale jump-to-message results.

UI · packages/ui/src/screens · part 1 of 2

JoinScreen.tsx

Join / sign-in screen · 989 lines · changed in 20 commits

The first screen for a new device: pick or find a workspace, then sign in or create an account. It lists saved workspaces, workspaces found on the LAN, a direct-address box, and on desktop an offer to resume or start hosting. Once credentials are accepted it calls onConnected with a SavedServer.

How it works

  • Stages: browse, probing (calling /server-info on an address) and auth (sign-in/register card).
  • On the web it quietly asks its own origin for server info; if the page is served by a workspace and nothing else is saved, it jumps straight to that workspace's sign-in card.
  • Saved workspaces reconnect with their stored token (Api.me); only a 401 falls back to the sign-in card.

Optimizations here

  • A probe attempt counter drops results from slower or cancelled probes.
  • Avoids flashing the full list on the web until the self-origin check answers.
  • LAN results already in the saved list are filtered out with useMemo.

UI · packages/ui/src/lib · part 1 of 2

deviceStore.ts

Web device storage (IndexedDB + journal) · 687 lines · changed in 3 commits

The web client's durable key-value store for sign-ins, drafts, outbox and preferences. It uses IndexedDB, where every change is one read-merge-write transaction serialised across all tabs, and writes each change first to a small localStorage journal so a closing page's last change is replayed on next start. Other tabs are told about changes over a BroadcastChannel.

How it works

  • Changes are data (StoreOp: set, initialize, outbox, drafts, record) so they can be journaled and replayed; applyOp uses client-core's merge helpers.
  • Database "tandem-device" v2 has two object stores: values (stored JSON text) and made (per key, the last sequence number each tab applied).
  • Each tab gets a random id and an increasing seq; the made record makes replayed changes idempotent, and entries older than 30 days are pruned unless still journaled.

Optimizations here

  • One IndexedDB readwrite transaction per change gives cross-tab atomic merges.
  • Synchronous localStorage journal makes the last write of a closing page survive.
  • Per-tab sequence numbers make journal replay idempotent.
  • localStorage backend skips the write when the serialised value is unchanged.

UI · packages/ui/src/lib · part 2 of 2

deviceStore.ts

Web device storage (IndexedDB + journal) · 687 lines · changed in 3 commits

How it works (continued)

  • On startup, journal entries (slackoss-journal:<tab>:<seq>) are validated, sorted and applied before anything else; invalid entries are deleted.
  • OWNER_KEY records whether this profile uses indexeddb or localstorage; once IndexedDB has been used, localStorage alone is refused rather than silently giving an empty store.
  • Values left in old localStorage keys (slackoss:<key>) are migrated inside the same transaction; conflicting drafts/outbox/notification-preview copies are reconciled (merged, keeping the more private preview).
  • openDatabase times out after 5 seconds and rejects on blocked/version issues, so a stuck IndexedDB reports unreadability instead of hanging.
  • watch() listens to BroadcastChannel messages, storage events (fallback invalidation via CHANGE_KEY) and window focus, using a generation counter to drop stale refreshes.

More optimizations

  • 5-second open timeout prevents the app hanging on a broken IndexedDB.
  • Cross-tab change notification by BroadcastChannel, with storage-event and focus refresh as fallback.

UI · packages/ui/src · part 1 of 2

App.tsx

Root component and session router · 547 lines · changed in 20 commits

The top of the React tree. It restores saved sign-ins from platform storage, then shows either the Join screen or the Workspace screen, and handles deep links, hosting status and the 'forget saved sign-ins' recovery path. It owns the single live WorkspaceClient and destroys it whenever the view changes.

How it works

  • Session is a small state machine: loading -> restore_failed | join | workspace (workspace carries the WorkspaceClient, SavedServer and an optional message target).
  • On mount, restoreServers reads the "servers" key with strict:true and validates it with parseSavedServers; an unreadable store shows a 'Saved sign-ins could not be opened' card instead of silently treating it as empty.
  • If the most recent saved server is a workspace this computer hosted but has stopped (hostedButStopped), it shows Join (to offer restarting) instead of reconnecting forever.

Optimizations here

  • JoinScreen is React.lazy-loaded: returning users open straight into a workspace and never download it.
  • HostDialog is lazy-loaded since only desktop users open it, and only occasionally.
  • Navigation tickets and save-version counters discard stale async results instead of letting them race.

UI · packages/ui/src · part 2 of 2

App.tsx

Root component and session router · 547 lines · changed in 20 commits

How it works (continued)

  • openWorkspace destroys the previous client, creates a new WorkspaceClient(url, token), connects, and moves that server to the front of the saved list with a fresh lastUsedAt.
  • handleDeepLink: a message link to the open workspace just changes the target without reconnecting; to a known server it reconnects with saved credentials; otherwise it goes to Join with autoProbe and remembers the target until sign-in completes.
  • A ticket counter (navigation ref) is bumped on every navigation so late async results (storage reads, hosting start, deferred links) cannot override a newer choice.
  • Save failures show a non-blocking banner with Retry; persistServers uses a version counter so only the latest save clears or sets the error.
  • Wraps everything in PlatformContext, ErrorBoundary, ToastProvider and ConfirmProvider; on desktop it shows a hosting status bar with a Manage hosting button.

More optimizations

  • A deep link to a message in the already-open workspace updates the target in place rather than reconnecting.
  • Forgetting sign-ins defers any deep link that arrives mid-operation and replays it afterwards.

Optimizations: - JoinScreen is React.lazy-loaded: returning users open straight into a workspace and never download it. - HostDialog is lazy-loaded since only desktop users open it, and only occasionally. - Navigation tickets and save-version counters discard stale async results instead of letting them race. - A deep link to a message in the already-open workspace updates the target in place rather than reconnecting. - Forgetting sign-ins defers any deep link that arrives mid-operation and replays it afterwards. UI · packages/ui/src · part 1 of 2

platform.ts

Platform abstraction (web vs desktop) · 406 lines · changed in 32 commits

Defines the Platform interface: everything the surrounding shell (browser or Electron) gives the UI - storage, notifications, downloads, deep links, LAN discovery and workspace hosting. It also implements webPlatform(), the browser version backed by the IndexedDB device store.

How it works

  • Platform.kind is "desktop" or "web"; most capabilities are optional so the web client degrades gracefully (no LAN discovery, no hosting).
  • storage has get/set plus optional atomic helpers: initialize, mergeOutbox, mergeDrafts, mergeRecord, and watchOutbox/watchDrafts/watchRecord for cross-window changes.
  • get accepts { strict: true } so callers can tell 'unreadable' apart from 'nothing stored'.
  • hosting (desktop only) covers start/stop, public address via Cloudflare Tunnel, invite-only, backups, auto-backup schedules, restore, rename, ports, start-on-launch and open-at-login.

Optimizations here

  • Atomic merge operations (mergeOutbox, mergeDrafts, mergeRecord) let multiple windows write one key without losing each other's changes.
  • Notification tags deduplicate the same alert across tabs of one account.

UI · packages/ui/src · part 2 of 2

platform.ts

Platform abstraction (web vs desktop) · 406 lines · changed in 32 commits

How it works (continued)

  • webPlatform storage maps every call to deviceStore().apply with an op kind (set, initialize, outbox, drafts, record).
  • webPlatform.downloadFile loads the URL in a hidden no-referrer iframe, removed after 5 minutes, so a failed download cannot replace the app page.
  • webPlatform.notify uses the browser Notification API only when permission is granted, and passes a tag so several tabs show one notification.
  • Web deep links come from the page address (#/join/... or #/c/.../m/...); takeLinkFromAddress strips the fragment with history.replaceState so a reload or the history does not keep an invite code.

UI · packages/ui/src · part 1 of 2

theme.css

Design tokens and global styles · 382 lines · changed in 12 commits

The Tailwind v4 theme and global stylesheet for the whole UI. It defines the colour, font and surface tokens for the dark 'Onyx' theme and the 'White' light theme, compact density, responsive layout breakpoints and a few component classes.

How it works

  • A header comment documents the design system: surface order, the allowed type scale, spacing, radius scale and focus ring; theme.test.ts enforces the type and radius scales.
  • Onyx (dark) is the default; :root[data-theme="light"] and a prefers-color-scheme media query for data-theme="system" swap in the White palette.
  • The accent token keeps the name --color-copper for compatibility; it is ChaiCode orange in Onyx and a deepened orange in White for 4.5:1 contrast.
  • :root[data-density="compact"] shrinks body and message text and tightens message and channel rows.

Optimizations here

  • .timeline-scroll uses overscroll-behavior: contain and overflow-anchor: none to control scrolling in the message list.
  • Theme and density switch by changing a data attribute on <html>, with no re-render of components.

UI shell, screens and helpers · 1–2 of 39 smaller files

workspaceStorage.ts and route.ts

workspaceStorage.ts

Account-scoped workspace storage · 405 lines

Builds storage keys scoped to a workspace and account, and provides read, write, update and merge operations for workspace data (drafts, outbox, other values). It serialises operations per key, migrates data from older address-based keys, and uses the platform's atomic merges when available.

  • Keys look like local:v1:<workspaceId>:<selfId>:<kind>[:<suffix>]; the legacy key was <kind>:<baseUrl>:<selfId>.
  • New-style values are wrapped as { version: 1, value } (an envelope) so unreadable data can be detected.

Optimization: Per-key promise queue (serialized) prevents lost updates within a window, and starts uncontended operations synchronously so a pagehide save is not delayed.

route.ts

URL hash and history routing · 254 lines

Encodes where someone is in a workspace (channel, thread or side panel, dialog, phone drawer, scroll position) into the URL hash and history state, and reads it back, so Back, Forward and reload return to the same place.

  • Hash format: #/c/<channel>[/t/<thread> | /p/<panel>][/d/<dialog>[/<account section>]].
  • Panels: pins, saved, threads, scheduled, activity; dialogs: account, people, apps, invite, shortcuts, details.

Optimization: Skips history writes when the route or rounded scroll position has not changed.

packages/ui/src/lib/workspaceStorage.ts (405 lines, changed in 7 commits, added 2026-09-12, last changed 2026-10-02). Builds storage keys scoped to a workspace and account, and provides read, write, update and merge operations for workspace data (drafts, outbox, other values). It serialises operations per key, migrates data from older address-based keys, and uses the platform's atomic merges when available. How it works: - Keys look like local:v1:<workspaceId>:<selfId>:<kind>[:<suffix>]; the legacy key was <kind>:<baseUrl>:<selfId>. - New-style values are wrapped as { version: 1, value } (an envelope) so unreadable data can be detected. - On first read, a value under a legacy key is moved across only from addresses trusted via checkWorkspaceAddress, then the old key is cleared. - initialize() stores a value only if nothing is there (atomically where the platform supports it), so a window cannot overwrite another window's newer write; absence is also recorded so stale legacy data cannot come back later. - Outbox and drafts are always merged, never overwritten wholesale; legacy drafts only fill conversations without a draft. - mergeWorkspaceOutbox and mergeWorkspaceDraftsAtOnce call the platform's merge immediately (not after the queue) so a closing page can still save. - updateWorkspaceStorage does read-modify-write in one queue turn; an unreadable value is replaced instead of blocking saves. Optimizations: - Per-key promise queue (serialized) prevents lost updates within a window, and starts uncontended operations synchronously so a pagehide save is not delayed. - Uses platform-level atomic merges across windows when available. - Failed operations do not block later ones in the queue. - mergeWorkspaceDrafts skips the write when there are no changes. UI shell, screens and helpers · 3–4 of 39 smaller files

deeplink.ts and notificationPreview.ts

deeplink.ts

Deep link parsing and building · 198 lines

Parses and builds links that join a workspace or open a message, in both the desktop form (tandem://join?host=...) and the browser form (<server>/#/join/<code>). Also chooses the best address to put in a link someone else will open.

  • parseDeepLink accepts tandem:// and older protocol names (from DEEP_LINK_PROTOCOLS), plus http(s) root URLs with a #/join/<code> or #/c/<channel>/m/<message> fragment; returns null for anything malformed.
  • IDs and codes must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.
  • The browser form keeps the target in the fragment so invite codes are never sent to the server or in a Referer.

notificationPreview.ts

Notification privacy preference store · 197 lines

Stores, per account, how much a message notification shows: the full message, only sender and channel, or nothing. Builds notification title/body for single messages and catch-up summaries, and defaults to the most private option whenever the choice is unknown.

  • Stored under "notification-previews" as a record of account -> choice; account key is '<serverUrl> <userId>'.
  • Damaged entries are read as "none" and flagged; a special "*" entry keeps unknown accounts private after storage damage.

Optimization: Per-key record merge avoids one window overwriting another window's choices.

diagnostics.ts and workspaceAddressTrust.ts

diagnostics.ts

Diagnostics report text · 145 lines

Builds the plain-text diagnostics report people can copy for support: app and server versions, connection, device and (for admins) server health. It never includes message content, names or tokens.

  • Lines cover app type, protocol and build, server version/protocol/build or why it was unreachable, address, connection status, offline state, messages waiting to send (count only), huddle peers, notification permission, window size and user agent.

workspaceAddressTrust.ts

Trusted workspace addresses · 127 lines

Records which server addresses this device has linked to a workspace and account. Local work saved under an old address is only brought across to addresses that were trusted, so a server copying a workspace's ID cannot read someone's local data.

  • Key: local:v1:<workspaceId>:<userId>:trusted-addresses, value { version: 1, addresses }.
  • normalizeWorkspaceAddress keeps protocol, port and path, rejects credentials, query and fragment, and strips trailing slashes.

Optimization: Per-key promise queue prevents concurrent read-modify-write races.

UI shell, screens and helpers · 7–8 of 39 smaller files

callPreferences.ts and useRovingMessages.ts

callPreferences.ts

Huddle join preference store · 125 lines

Stores whether this device joins huddles muted, and provides joinHuddle, which waits for that preference before joining. Anything unknown or unreadable keeps the microphone off.

  • Stored under "call-preferences"; read with strict:true and validated, so corrupt data counts as unreadable instead of absent.
  • Defaults to joinMuted: true until storage answers or when it cannot be read.
  • A load version counter means an explicit user choice supersedes any older, slower read.

Optimization: Version counter discards stale preference reads.

useRovingMessages.ts

Roving tabindex for message lists · 112 lines

Makes a message list a single Tab stop: only the current message and its controls are tabbable; arrow keys, Home and End move between messages, Enter goes into the message's toolbar, Escape comes back out.

  • Messages are elements with role="article"; until someone moves, the current message is the newest.
  • Controls in non-current messages get tabIndex -1 and a data-roving-out marker so they can be restored later; controls with their own tabindex are left alone.
  • A MutationObserver re-applies the tab order when messages are added, removed or changed without a React render.

Optimization: Tab passes the whole list in a few presses instead of hundreds.

recentSearches.ts and appearance.ts

recentSearches.ts

Recent searches hook · 102 lines

Keeps the last 10 searches (query and optional channel) for this account in this workspace on this device, with add, remove and clear.

  • Key is workspaceStorageKey(baseUrl, workspaceId, selfId, "recent-searches").
  • parse() drops invalid entries, queries over 200 characters, empty entries and duplicates, and stops at 10.
  • All reads and writes for a key are chained on one promise queue per platform, so a late append cannot undo a clear even across closed and reopened dialogs.

Optimization: Per-key promise queue serialises storage operations.

appearance.ts

Theme and density preference store · 95 lines

Holds the device's chosen theme (system, dark, light) and density (comfortable, compact) in a zustand store saved through platform storage. useApplyAppearance writes them onto <html> as data attributes that theme.css reads.

  • Stored under the "appearance" key; defaults to dark (Onyx) and comfortable.
  • One store per Platform, cached in a WeakMap, so every component shares it.
  • set() applies the change immediately (optimistic) and rolls back with an error message if saving fails.

Optimization: Optimistic update makes the choice feel instant; rollback on storage failure.

messageReferences.ts

Per-message user/channel lookups · 87 lines

Works out which users and channels one message row needs (author, mentions, reactors, mentioned channels, linked messages' channels) and subscribes to only those entries in the workspace store.

  • Scans text for <@user> and <#channel> tokens and for http(s) links that parse as message deep links.
  • Includes every user id that reacted to the message.
  • usePick builds a selector that returns the same object until one of the picked entries changes.

Optimization: Selector does no work when the users/channels map object is unchanged (most updates: typing, presence).

useCopy.ts

Clipboard copy hook · 83 lines

Copies text to the clipboard and reports 'copied' only if it actually worked, falling back to the older selection + execCommand method where the Clipboard API is missing or refused (common on plain-http LAN workspaces).

  • useCopy returns copy(text, key), label(idle, done, failed, key) and copied; state resets after resetMs (default 1.5 s).
  • writeClipboard tries navigator.clipboard.writeText, then copySelection.

catchUp.ts and localWork.ts

catchUp.ts

Reconnect catch-up summary · 82 lines

Collects messages missed while disconnected and, once the replay goes quiet, shows them as one summary instead of one notification each. Also formats a short list of names.

  • hold(message) stores a message and (re)starts a timer; the replay counts as finished after 1 second of quiet.
  • At most one summary per workspace every 2 minutes; a later catch-up waits until that interval has passed.
  • On flush it keeps only messages still worth telling (stillNews), sorts by seq and calls show; if none remain, the interval is not consumed.

Optimization: Debounces and rate-limits notifications after a reconnect instead of firing one per missed message.

localWork.ts

Local persistence ledger for sends · 81 lines

Tracks whether a message just sent has been safely stored on the device (in the outbox or as a saved draft), so the composer can keep the text until it is. Components that persist work register as 'keepers'.

  • One ledger per WorkspaceClient, kept in a WeakMap: a keeper count and a map of send nonces to waiting listeners.
  • whenKeptLocally returns null when no keeper exists; otherwise a promise that resolves 'stored' or 'unsaved', timing out to 'unsaved' after 5 seconds.
  • When the last keeper unregisters, every waiting send is settled as 'unsaved'.

Optimization: WeakMap keyed by client lets ledgers be garbage-collected with the client.

UI shell, screens and helpers · 15–16 of 39 smaller files

textInput.ts and format.ts

textInput.ts

Text field input rules · 80 lines

Rules every text field follows before acting on a key: ignore keys that belong to an input method (IME), keep Enter inside an open code block, and only restore a caret position if the text has not changed since.

  • isImeKey checks isComposing or keyCode 229, so Enter used to pick a CJK candidate does not send a message.
  • insideCodeBlock counts fences before the caret; an odd count means Enter adds a line instead of sending.
  • caretToRestore returns null if the field text differs from when the position was computed, so a fast typist's caret is not dragged backwards.
  • Returned positions are clamped to the current text length.

format.ts

Formatting helpers · 77 lines

Small display helpers: byte sizes, times and days, conversation titles, avatar colours and initials.

  • formatBytes shows B/KB/MB/GB with one decimal under 10.
  • formatDay returns Today, Yesterday, or a weekday-month-day string.
  • channelTitle names DMs and group DMs by the other members' display names (or yourself for a self-DM).
  • avatarColor hashes the user id to one of 8 hues in oklch at a lightness that keeps white initials at 4.5:1 contrast; alpha < 1 gives a tint.

Optimization: Intl.DateTimeFormat instances are created once at module load and reused, since a time is formatted for every message on screen.

hosting.ts and useTabs.ts

hosting.ts

Hosting status hooks · 76 lines

React hooks that read the desktop app's hosting status (live, via subscribe plus an initial read) and the last workspace hosted on this computer.

  • useHostingStatus returns { status, loading, error, refresh }; it does nothing on the web, where platform.hosting is absent.
  • A revision counter makes a live subscription update win over an older in-flight status read.
  • loading is reported only for the first read, so refreshing does not blank controls already on screen.
  • useLastHosted re-reads platform.hosting.lastHosted whenever the hosting phase or the running workspace changes.

Optimization: Revision counter drops stale status reads.

useTabs.ts

WAI-ARIA tabs hook · 72 lines

Implements the accessible tabs pattern: one tab stop, arrow keys with wrap, Home/End, selection follows focus, and a single shared panel.

  • Returns listProps (tablist with a label), tabProps(tab) and panelProps.
  • Only the selected tab has tabIndex 0; onSelect is called only for a different tab and says whether a key or click chose it.
  • Keys with Alt, Ctrl or Meta are ignored so Alt+Left still means Back.

useListbox.ts and coalescedLoader.ts

useListbox.ts

Listbox/combobox accessibility hook · 66 lines

Gives a text box a list of suggestions navigable with arrow keys while focus stays in the box, using aria-activedescendant. Used by the quick switcher, composer suggestions and emoji choosers.

  • Returns active index, choose, move(event), ownerProps (for a textarea), comboboxProps (for an input), listProps and optionProps(i).
  • ArrowUp/ArrowDown wrap around; Left/Right/Home/End are left to the text box.
  • Options set the choice on mouse enter and prevent default on mouse down so the caret stays in the box.

Optimization: Scrolls the active option into view only after a key press, not on pointer hover.

coalescedLoader.ts

Coalescing list loader · 64 lines

A small class that keeps a list fresh without piling up requests. Direct requests load immediately and cancel any in-flight load; 'may be stale' signals are debounced so at most one load runs and one waits.

  • now(): clears any timer, aborts the in-flight load via AbortController and starts a new one.
  • soon(): if a load is running, marks one more load as queued; otherwise starts a single debounce timer (delayMs).
  • When a load finishes and a load was queued, it runs once more.

Optimization: Coalesces bursts of invalidation events into one request.

Composer Enter-key preference store · 64 lines

Stores whether Enter sends a message or inserts a new line, shared by every composer on the device and saved through platform storage.

  • Stored under "composer-preferences" as { enterSends }.
  • Until storage answers, enterSends is false, so an early Enter adds a new line instead of sending by accident.
  • Once loaded with nothing saved, the default is Enter sends.
  • setEnterSends is ignored until loaded or while a save is in progress; failures set an error message.
  • One zustand store per Platform, cached in a WeakMap.

Optimization: WeakMap-cached shared store per platform.

lastConversation.ts

Last-open conversation hook · 63 lines

Remembers which conversation this account last had open in this workspace on this device, so the app can reopen it on next start.

  • Key is built with workspaceStorageKey(baseUrl, workspaceId, selfId, "last-conversation") without a legacy slot.
  • remembered is undefined while reading and null when nothing (valid) is saved; values must match the channel id pattern.
  • remember(channelId) skips the write if the same value was just written, and ignores failures (losing it costs one click).

Optimization: Deduplicates repeated writes of the same conversation.

UI shell, screens and helpers · 23–24 of 39 smaller files

resume.ts and schedule.ts

resume.ts

Resume-hosting detection · 63 lines

Detects when a saved workspace is the one this computer hosted last and hosting is stopped, so the app offers to start hosting it again instead of reconnecting forever.

  • resumeTarget matches a saved server by loopback address and port (not by name), and only when hosting is not running, starting or stopping.
  • An empty port (default web port) never counts as a hosted workspace.
  • hostedButStopped reads hosting status and lastHosted in parallel and answers false on any error.

Optimization: Reads status and lastHosted with Promise.all.

schedule.ts

Scheduled message time helpers · 62 lines

Preset times and formatting for scheduling a message: in 30 minutes, in an hour, this evening, tomorrow morning, Monday morning.

  • 'This evening' (18:00) is offered only if it is more than an hour away.
  • Monday morning skips to next week if today is Monday; mornings are 9:00 local time.
  • localDateTime formats a value for datetime-local inputs without converting to UTC.
  • formatScheduleTime reads 'Today at ...', 'Tomorrow at ...', or a weekday and date.

emoji.ts

Emoji list and search · 61 lines

The fixed set of 48 emoji offered by the composer's emoji chooser and the reaction picker, each with search words, and a search function.

  • Each entry is [emoji, words]; the words also name the emoji's button for screen readers.
  • findEmoji matches a lower-cased substring of the words, or the emoji itself if pasted.

usePanelFocus.ts

Side panel focus management hook · 59 lines

Moves focus into a side panel when it opens and gives it back to whatever opened it when it closes, for keyboard and screen-reader users.

  • Captures the opener (document.activeElement) during render, before anything inside the panel takes focus.
  • With takeFocus, focuses the panel heading, except when the opener is a toggle button (aria-pressed/expanded) that stays visible; on a phone where the opener is inert it still focuses the heading.
  • On close, returns focus only if focus was lost or inside the panel.
  • handBack falls back to the nearest focusable ancestor, then to an element named by data-focus-fallback.

connection.ts and account.ts

connection.ts

Connection error explanations · 58 lines

Explains why a workspace did not answer, and whether a server is compatible with this app, in specific plain-English messages.

  • connectionFailure separates 401/403 (credentials refused), other HTTP errors, an https page blocked from an http address (mixed content), a TimeoutError, and plain unreachability.
  • pageProtocol is passed in rather than read from window, so the logic is testable without a browser.
  • incompatibleWorkspace checks info.app === "slackoss" and compares protocolVersion with PROTOCOL_VERSION to say which side must update.
  • host() strips http(s):// for use in sentences.

account.ts

Account error and device labels · 53 lines

Turns account-management API errors into readable sentences and turns a session's user-agent string into a short device label.

  • accountError maps ApiError codes such as invalid_credentials, auth_busy, owner_only, admins_are_equals and bots_have_no_password to specific messages.
  • Non-API errors get a 'check your connection and refresh' message, since the change may or may not have happened.
  • deviceLabel detects Tandem desktop (Electron), Edge, Firefox, Chrome, Safari and the OS (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux), e.g. 'Chrome · Windows'.

savedServers.ts and context.ts

savedServers.ts

Saved sign-ins validator · 37 lines

Validates the stored list of saved sign-ins. A corrupt value throws instead of becoming an empty list that a later save would overwrite.

  • null means nothing saved and returns [].
  • Each entry must have string url, non-empty token, workspaceName and handle, and a finite non-negative lastUsedAt.
  • URL must be http(s) with no username, password, query or fragment.
  • Returns clean objects with only the known fields.

context.ts

React contexts and store hooks · 34 lines

Defines the React contexts that carry the Platform, the current WorkspaceClient and an 'open this message' callback down the tree. Provides hooks to read them, including useWorkspace, which subscribes a component to a slice of the client's zustand store.

  • usePlatform and useClient throw if their provider is missing, so misuse fails loudly.
  • useWorkspace(selector) wraps zustand's useStore(client.store, selector): a component re-renders only when its selected slice changes.

Optimization: Selector-based subscriptions to the workspace replica avoid re-rendering components on unrelated state changes.

historyKeys.ts and threadPosition.ts

historyKeys.ts

Back/Forward keyboard and mouse hook · 30 lines

On the desktop app, which has no browser toolbar, makes Alt+Left/Right and the mouse side buttons go Back and Forward in history.

  • Ignores events already handled or combined with Ctrl, Meta or Shift.
  • Mouse buttons 3 and 4 map to history.back and history.forward on mouseup.
  • Enabled only when passed true (WorkspaceScreen passes platform.kind === "desktop").

threadPosition.ts

In-memory thread scroll positions · 30 lines

Remembers where each thread was left (top reply and offset) for as long as the app runs, so reopening a thread returns there instead of to the newest reply.

  • Keyed by '<serverUrl> <rootId>' in a module-level Map.
  • Passing null (at the newest reply) forgets the position.
  • Keeps at most 100 threads; re-inserting a key moves it to the end, and the oldest is evicted.

Optimization: LRU-style cap of 100 entries using Map insertion order bounds memory.

Area 6 of 14 · packages/ui/src/components

UI components

The components are flat files in one folder, mostly one feature each (Composer, MessageTimeline, Sidebar, HostDialog), with a few files grouping related pieces (dialogs.tsx for new-channel/browse/new-DM/invite dialogs, MessageListPanel.tsx for the Pinned, Saved and Threads panels). They get workspace state through hooks in ../context.ts: useClient() returns the client-core WorkspaceClient (API calls and actions such as send, markRead, toggleReaction) and useWorkspace(selector) subscribes to narrow slices of its Zustand store, while usePlatform() reaches web or desktop specifics like storage, downloads and hosting; reusable behaviour lives in ../lib hooks (useListbox, useTabs, usePanelFocus, useRovingMessages, useCopy, workspaceStorage). Shared primitives are Modal (one focus-trapping, inert-making layer used by every overlay), Dialog (the titled shell on Modal, plus the shared inputCls), Menu (an action menu on the modal layer), Button/buttonClass (four variants), Tooltip, Icon (inline SVG paths), Avatar, ListStatus (loading/empty/error states), and the context-provided services Confirm (useConfirm), Toast (useToast) and ShareableServer. Side panels and dialogs can be code-split and wrapped in LazyPanel/LazyDialog, and ErrorBoundary keeps a crashed view from taking down the workspace.

UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 1 of 2

HostDialog.tsx

Host a workspace (desktop) · 1,896 lines · changed in 23 commits

The desktop app's hosting dialog, where this computer becomes the Tandem server. When nothing is running it lists workspaces hosted here (start, rename, change port, back up, open folder, restore from backup, 'Look inside' / 'Put back in use' for restored copies) and lets you start a new one; when one is running it shows the network addresses, port, connected count, data folder, automatic backups, start-with-computer options and the 'Open to all' public link.

How it works

  • Talks only to the Platform 'hosting' interface (start, stop, list, backup, restore, rename, setPort, openToAll, setPublicAddress, setInviteOnly, setAutoBackup, openAtLogin and more); optional functions hide their UI when the platform lacks them.
  • An operationPending ref plus a 'busy' state allow one operation at a time, and the dialog cannot be dismissed while one runs.

Optimizations here

  • The hosted workspace list is re-read only when the hosting phase changes or a revision counter is bumped after an operation.
  • Status refresh and dialog open share one refresh function from useHostingStatus.

Composer.tsx

Message input · 1,056 lines · changed in 36 commits

The message box at the bottom of a channel or thread. You type with formatting, @-mentions and /commands, attach files by button, drag-and-drop or paste, preview the formatted text, and send now or schedule for later; replies can also be sent to the channel. Drafts are saved per conversation (threads have their own slot) and survive switching conversations and closing the window.

How it works

  • Enter sends or adds a new line depending on the device preference (useComposerPreferences); Ctrl/Cmd+Enter always sends; Enter inside a code block adds a line; IME composition keys are ignored; Ctrl+B/I/E format the selection.
  • @ opens a mention list (people plus @channel/@here in rooms only, max 6) with NFC-normalised matching; Enter/Tab inserts a <@id> or <!token>, Escape closes it. A leading '/' word shows matching slash commands (max 6), completed with Tab.
  • Drafts are written to the client store 250 ms after typing stops, flushed on conversation switch (layout-effect cleanup), page hide and desktop close, and taken on from other windows unless there is unsaved typing here.

Optimizations here

  • Draft saving debounced by 250 ms; typing notifications throttled to one per 3 seconds.
  • The schedule-request validation schema (@slackoss/protocol/rest) is loaded with a dynamic import() only when a saved request exists, since it pulls in a validation library that is a sizeable part of the bundle.
  • useMemo for mention candidates, command candidates and the storage key.

UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 2 of 2

Composer.tsx

Message input · 1,056 lines · changed in 36 commits

How it works (continued)

  • Sending calls client.send; a refused send (e.g. outbox full at OUTBOX_LIMIT) keeps the text and explains why. The words stay in the box, read-only, until whenKeptLocally confirms the send is stored on the device (GL-02).
  • Send later offers presets or a datetime-local picker; it uploads attachments, saves the exact request (with a random nonce) to device storage before submitting, and offers 'Retry confirmation' so a retry can never queue a duplicate.
  • Attachments are capped at 10 files; a clipboard holding both a file and text attaches the file and says the text was not pasted.
  • Typing indicators are sent at most once every 3 seconds (client.sendTyping); a character counter appears within 1,000 characters of MESSAGE_LIMIT.
  • Archived channels disable the box with an explanation; the textarea auto-grows up to 220px and the caret is restored in a layout effect after programmatic edits.

More optimizations

  • Uploaded file ids are cached in a WeakMap so retrying a schedule does not re-upload the same files.
  • Refs for the latest typed text and edit state avoid re-subscribing effects on every keystroke.

AccountDialog.tsx

Account settings · 849 lines · changed in 15 commits

The 'Account settings' dialog with a vertical tab list of sections: Profile, Notifications, Appearance, Composing, Calls, Security, Devices and Storage. It covers editing your profile, notification permission, pausing and previews, theme and density, Enter-to-send, joining huddles muted with a mic test, changing password and signing out, managing signed-in devices, and viewing workspace storage use.

How it works

  • The section list is an ARIA tablist (vertical) with roving tabIndex; Arrow keys, Home and End move between sections with wraparound.
  • The open section can be driven from outside (Back/Forward) via the section prop, and onSectionChange reports changes so the URL can follow.
  • Password change checks that the new passwords match and differ from the current one, then signs out other devices (client.api.changePassword).

Optimizations here

  • Session loads use a version counter so only the newest response is applied; load is a stable useCallback.
  • Only the selected section's content is rendered.

UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 1 of 2

HuddleStage.tsx

Huddle video stage · 704 lines · changed in 3 commits

The video area for a huddle with cameras or screen shares. It sits above the chat at a draggable height, can expand over the chat or go full screen, and shows either an equal-size gallery or a spotlight (a shared screen or pinned person large, everyone else in a strip).

How it works

  • bestFit tries every column count to find the largest 16:9 tile that fits N tiles in the available box.
  • stageItems orders shared screens first, then you, then other participants; each tile shows the camera, or an avatar on a colour glow when the camera is off, plus name, muted icon, a 'Connecting…' overlay and a green ring while speaking.
  • Video elements are always muted because audio plays separately (HuddleAudio), avoiding doubled voices; your own camera is mirrored.
  • When you are the one sharing, a 'Presenting' panel with a small preview and Stop sharing replaces a full-size view of your own screen, adapting to tall, wide or small layouts.

Optimizations here

  • useElementSize uses a ResizeObserver and skips state updates when the size has not changed.
  • Renders nothing in calls without video (the huddle bar covers that case).

packages/ui/src/components/HuddleStage.tsx (704 lines, changed in 3 commits, added 2026-09-19, last changed 2026-09-26). The video area for a huddle with cameras or screen shares. It sits above the chat at a draggable height, can expand over the chat or go full screen, and shows either an equal-size gallery or a spotlight (a shared screen or pinned person large, everyone else in a strip). How it works: - bestFit tries every column count to find the largest 16:9 tile that fits N tiles in the available box. - stageItems orders shared screens first, then you, then other participants; each tile shows the camera, or an avatar on a colour glow when the camera is off, plus name, muted icon, a 'Connecting…' overlay and a green ring while speaking. - Video elements are always muted because audio plays separately (HuddleAudio), avoiding doubled voices; your own camera is mirrored. - When you are the one sharing, a 'Presenting' panel with a small preview and Stop sharing replaces a full-size view of your own screen, adapting to tall, wide or small layouts. - Tiles can be pinned (button or double-click); a pin of someone who left, or a grid with nothing to spotlight, is cleared automatically. - The resize handle is a focusable role=separator with aria-valuenow; drag with pointer capture or use Arrow keys (5% steps) and Home/End, limited to 20–80% of the column. - In full screen the HuddleControls overlay and the cursor hide after 3 seconds without pointer or key activity; focus inside the controls keeps them visible. - If someone starts sharing while the video is hidden, the stage switches back to docked. Optimizations: - useElementSize uses a ResizeObserver and skips state updates when the size has not changed. - Renders nothing in calls without video (the huddle bar covers that case). UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 1 of 2

DraftPersistence.tsx

Local drafts and outbox persistence · 695 lines · changed in 14 commits

An invisible component that saves unsent work (composer drafts and the queue of messages waiting to send) to this device, scoped to the workspace and account, and restores it after a restart. It also keeps several open windows of the same account in sync without one overwriting another's work; it only renders an error banner with Retry or a notice when drafts conflict.

How it works

  • On start it reads stored drafts, the stored outbox and an 'unstored-sends' key in parallel, merges them with what the client already holds, and hydrates the client (client.hydrateDrafts, client.restoreOutbox).
  • Each window writes only the drafts it changed, with the text they changed from, so a draft changed meanwhile in another window is kept beside this one (keepBothDrafts, GL-03) and a notice says both versions were kept.
  • Outbox entries get revisions; writes merge through mergeWorkspaceOutbox, and tombstones record sends delivered or discarded so other windows drop them too; a refusal seen in another window is adopted here (client.adoptRefusal).

Optimizations here

  • Draft writes are debounced by 600 ms after the last change; outbox changes are written immediately.
  • Only changed drafts are written, not the whole set.
  • Unchanged outbox entries are skipped by comparing their JSON; the unstored-sends key is rewritten only when its JSON changes.

UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 2 of 2

DraftPersistence.tsx

Local drafts and outbox persistence · 695 lines · changed in 14 commits

How it works (continued)

  • Re-writing to repair entries another window left out is capped at 3 attempts in a row so two windows cannot keep each other writing.
  • Drafts are written only after the outbox write before them succeeds, so a crash in between leaves the words in the composer rather than losing both.
  • While outbox writes fail, words of unstored sends are kept under their own key and put back into their composer on restart (once, as a draft or as a send, never both).
  • When the page hides or closes (pagehide, visibilitychange, platform.onPrepareClose) it writes immediately (F01); on desktop close it waits for all writes and refuses to close if anything is unsaved.
  • Works with lib/localWork (keepLocalWork/settleLocalWork) so sends wait until their words are stored on this device (GL-02).

More optimizations

  • Uses a raw client.store.subscribe instead of React state, so typing does not re-render this component.
  • Storage keys are memoised with useMemo.

ChannelDetailsDialog.tsx

Channel details and settings · 693 lines · changed in 13 commits

The dialog opened from a channel or conversation header with three tabs: About (name, topic, description, leave, archive/reopen), Members (list, add, remove, channel managers, change DM participants) and Notifications (notify level and mute).

How it works

  • Permissions come from shared protocol helpers (channelPermissions, canRemoveChannelMember, canSetChannelManager), so the UI offers only what the server allows; fields are read-only without manage rights.
  • channelError translates server codes such as name_taken, channel_management_required and channel_archived into plain sentences.
  • Members load from client.api.channelMembers with a Refresh/Retry attempt counter and ListStatus.
  • Leaving a private channel or group DM, archiving, removing a member and changing managers each need an inline confirmation that explains the consequence; #general cannot be left.

Optimizations here

  • NotificationSettings selects the stored prefs object and applies the default outside the selector, so the store subscription does not get a new object every render (as the code comment notes).

AppsDialog.tsx

Apps and integrations admin · 684 lines · changed in 13 commits

The admin dialog for creating and managing apps (bot integrations). For each app it shows the bot token (once) and signing secret, incoming webhooks per channel, slash commands, event subscriptions with delivery health, and the interactivity URL for message buttons.

How it works

  • Explains the Slack-compatible contract and links to docs/INTEGRATIONS.md for supported methods and differences.
  • Creating an app (client.api.createApp) inserts it immediately and keeps the one-time bot token visible for this session even if the follow-up list load fails.
  • Replacing a bot token, signing secret or webhook URL asks for confirmation with useConfirm, explaining what stops working.
  • SecretRow masks re-readable secrets behind Reveal and has a Copy button via useCopy; one-time secrets are labelled 'shown once'.
  • CommandList adds/removes slash commands and refreshes the composer's command hints with client.loadCommands().

Optimizations here

  • Load version counter ignores stale list responses; quiet reloads are skipped while one is already in flight.
  • Background polling (5 s) runs only while deliveries are pending.
  • load is a stable useCallback.

Sidebar.tsx

Workspace sidebar · 678 lines · changed in 26 commits

The left-hand navigation: a Discord-style rail of workspaces, the workspace name with a switcher menu, a 'Jump to…' button, shortcuts to Activity, Threads, Friends, Saved and Scheduled, the channel list, the direct message list, and a footer with your profile, a notification snooze control and a settings menu.

How it works

  • Channels are listed alphabetically; DMs and group DMs are sorted by most recent activity (channelLastSeq); archived and non-member channels are hidden.
  • Each ChannelRow shows unread (bold plus a left-edge nub), mention count badge, draft, muted and huddle-in-progress indicators, each with an accessible label.
  • Muted channels stay quiet: no unread nub, dimmed text.
  • Badges: Activity shows total mentions or the number of unread conversations, Threads shows unread followed threads (unreadThreadCount), Friends shows incoming requests.

Optimizations here

  • useMemo for splitting and sorting channels into rooms and DMs.
  • Many narrow useWorkspace selectors; the unread thread and friend request counts are computed inside selectors so they return plain numbers.

How it works: - Channels are listed alphabetically; DMs and group DMs are sorted by most recent activity (channelLastSeq); archived and non-member channels are hidden. - Each ChannelRow shows unread (bold plus a left-edge nub), mention count badge, draft, muted and huddle-in-progress indicators, each with an accessible label. - Muted channels stay quiet: no unread nub, dimmed text. - Badges: Activity shows total mentions or the number of unread conversations, Threads shows unread followed threads (unreadThreadCount), Friends shows incoming requests. - WorkspaceRail and WorkspaceSwitcher list this device's other saved sign-ins; same-named workspaces are told apart by handle and address. - WorkspaceMenu gathers Invite, People, Apps, Account settings, Keyboard shortcuts and Diagnostics in one Menu; People and Apps appear only when their callbacks are given (admins). - SnoozeControl offers Do Not Disturb durations (snoozeOptions) via client.snoozeNotificationsUntil; SnoozedNotice shows 'Paused until …' with Resume. - The active channel uses aria-current=page; the Jump button declares aria-keyshortcuts Control+K / Meta+K; the nav has data-focus-fallback for the mobile drawer. Optimizations: - useMemo for splitting and sorting channels into rooms and DMs. - Many narrow useWorkspace selectors; the unread thread and friend request counts are computed inside selectors so they return plain numbers. UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 1 of 2

MessageTimeline.tsx

Channel message timeline · 667 lines · changed in 21 commits

The scrolling list of messages in the open channel or DM. It groups messages by day and author, shows a 'New' line at the first unread message, loads older and newer history as you scroll, keeps your place, and also shows pending sends, private slash-command answers and who is typing.

How it works

  • Loads history through client.loadTimeline (initial/older) and client.loadNewer; a ticket object in a ref prevents overlapping requests and ignores stale results.
  • Stays pinned to the bottom when you are within 60px of it; a ResizeObserver keeps it pinned when side panels open or content rewraps.
  • When older messages are prepended or old ones are trimmed off the top, the first visible row is re-anchored so the view does not jump.
  • Back/Forward/reload restore the reading position saved by rememberReadingPosition (written on a 200 ms debounce and flushed on pagehide or leaving the channel).

Optimizations here

  • Wrapped in React.memo; each row is a memoised MessageItem.
  • Scroll position bookkeeping (pinnedToBottom, anchors, lastScrollTop) lives in refs, so scrolling does not trigger re-renders.
  • Reading-position writes are debounced by 200 ms.

UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 1 of 2

MessageItem.tsx

Single message row · 501 lines · changed in 23 commits

Renders one message in a channel or thread: avatar, name, time, formatted text, attachments, reactions, app buttons and reply count. On hover or focus a toolbar offers quick reactions, reply, copy link, save, mark unread, pin, edit and delete; the same actions are in a '...' menu for touchscreens.

How it works

  • Compact mode (consecutive messages from the same author) hides the avatar and header and shows the time on hover, positioned absolutely so the row height never changes.
  • Reactions, save and pin are optimistic toggles through the client; if the server refuses, a toast offers 'Try again' because the hover toolbar may be gone.
  • Delete asks for confirmation through useConfirm (destructive) and reports unconfirmed deletes inline.
  • Messages mentioning you get a highlighted background and copper left bar; jumped-to messages get a temporary highlight.

Optimizations here

  • Wrapped in React.memo so rows re-render only when their own props change.
  • useMessageReferences selects only the users and channels this message refers to, so unrelated store changes do not re-render the row.
  • Narrow selectors such as s.saved[message.id] and self role.

UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 1 of 2

Tooltip.tsx

Tooltip · 362 lines · changed in 3 commits

Small hover/focus hints for icon buttons, optionally showing a keyboard shortcut. It wraps a single child element, opens after a short hover delay or immediately on keyboard focus, and follows its trigger while scrolling.

How it works

  • Clones the child to add a merged ref, event handlers and aria-describedby pointing to the role=tooltip bubble, and removes the native title.
  • Hover opens after 400 ms; leaving waits 120 ms so the pointer can move onto the bubble; touch pointers are ignored.
  • Focus opens instantly unless the focus came from a mouse press; a pointer press hides it.
  • Only one tooltip is open at a time (module-level activeTooltip).
  • Escape (captured at document level) hides only the tooltip; window blur also hides it.

Optimizations here

  • Position updates write style only when values actually change, avoiding needless layout work.
  • Timers and hover/focus flags are kept in refs; callbacks are memoised with useCallback and the merged ref with useMemo.
  • Listeners, the ResizeObserver and the animation-frame follow loop run only while the tooltip is open.

UI · packages/ui/src/components · part 1 of 2

Modal.tsx

Modal layer (focus trap) · 335 lines · changed in 4 commits

The low-level modal layer under every dialog, menu and image viewer. It portals content to document.body, traps Tab inside the top-most layer, closes it on Escape or a click on the backdrop, makes everything else inert, and returns focus to the control that opened it.

How it works

  • Keeps a module-level set of open layers; the top-most is the one latest in document order.
  • While any layer is open, global keydown and focusin listeners and a MutationObserver on document.body are installed; they are removed when the last layer closes.
  • Sets the inert attribute on every other body child (remembering original values to restore), but skips the toast stack (data-tandem-toasts) so notices stay readable.
  • A MutationObserver on the active layer recovers focus if the focused element is removed, disabled or hidden, going to the last focused element or the panel.

Optimizations here

  • Global listeners and observers exist only while at least one modal is open.
  • The focus observer is filtered to a fixed list of attributes that can affect focusability.

UI components · 1–2 of 39 smaller files

dialogs.tsx and SearchDialog.tsx

dialogs.tsx

Channel, DM and invite dialogs · 526 lines

A collection of smaller workspace dialogs: create a new channel, browse and join channels, start a direct or group message, and invite people with invite codes and links.

  • NewChannelDialog turns the typed name into a lowercase hyphenated slug and creates a public or private channel via client.api.createChannel.
  • BrowseChannelsDialog filters public/private channels by name, can show archived ones, and offers Join (client.api.joinChannel) or Open.

Optimization: useMemo for the filtered channel list and for the user-permission signature string.

SearchDialog.tsx

Message search · 507 lines

The 'Search messages' dialog for full-text search across messages and attachment file names. Besides free text it offers filters for conversation, author, content type and date range, shows how the query was understood, keeps recent searches, and pages through results.

UI components · 3–4 of 39 smaller files

ScheduledPanel.tsx and PeopleDialog.tsx

ScheduledPanel.tsx

Scheduled messages panel · 465 lines

A side panel listing your messages queued to send later. For each one you can edit the text, cancel it, send it now, or change its delivery time; failed deliveries show the reason.

  • Loads with client.api.listScheduled and refreshes every 15 seconds while open, since entries disappear as they send.
  • Edit text saves via client.api.editScheduledMessage with the expected old text; a 'scheduled_changed' error means another device changed it, and the draft is kept.

Optimization: Polling refresh aborts the previous request with an AbortController.

PeopleDialog.tsx

Admin people management · 453 lines

The admin 'People' dialog listing every account with role, invite permission and last-seen date. Through a per-person actions menu, admins can change roles, allow or stop inviting, deactivate or reactivate accounts, reset passwords, and (owner only) transfer ownership.

  • Non-admins see only a message that owners and admins manage accounts.
  • Loads all users via client.api.listAllUsers and merges live user data from the store on top.
  • Actions the server would refuse (yourself, the owner, other admins when you are not owner) are not offered at all.

Optimization: load is a stable useCallback.

Attachments.tsx

File and image attachments · 396 lines

Shows files attached to messages: images as inline previews that open a full-size Lightbox, and other files as download cards with a type icon and size. Also shows attachments on messages still being sent, with an upload progress bar.

  • Images under 8 MB preview inline; larger images and other files show as FileCard download buttons.
  • Preview size is reserved from the stored width/height (capped at 380x300) using aspect-ratio, so the layout does not jump when the image loads.

Optimization: Lazy image loading: an IntersectionObserver (160px margin) only fetches a preview when it is near the viewport.

MessageListPanel.tsx

Pinned / Saved / Threads panels · 337 lines

A reusable side panel that lists a set of messages with paging, used for a channel's Pinned messages, your Saved items, and the Threads you follow. Each row shows the channel, author, a clamped preview and an 'Open' button that jumps to the message.

  • MessageListPanel takes a load(cursor, signal) function and a reloadKey; changing the key reloads from the first page.
  • Each load aborts the previous request with an AbortController; Retry repeats the exact last request.

Optimization: Reload keys are compact signature strings from narrow store selectors, so the panel refetches only when the relevant set changes.

ThreadPanel.tsx and Mrkdwn.tsx

ThreadPanel.tsx

Thread side panel · 330 lines

The side panel that shows a message's thread: the original message, its replies, a Follow toggle, and a reply composer at the bottom. It loads replies in pages, remembers where you were reading, and marks the thread read when you are at the newest reply.

  • Reads the thread page, replies, follow state and pending replies from the workspace store; the root falls back to the channel timeline until the thread page loads.

Optimization: Scroll restoration and anchoring done in useLayoutEffect before paint to avoid visible jumps.

Mrkdwn.tsx

Message text renderer · 284 lines

Turns Slack-style 'mrkdwn' message text into formatted React output: code blocks, inline code, bold, italic, strikethrough, quotes, @user and #channel mentions, @here/@channel, and links. It can also highlight search terms, and links to messages in this same workspace open in-app.

  • Splits on fences for code blocks, then groups '>' lines into blockquote runs, then tokenises inline syntax with one regex (INLINE_RE).
  • Backslash escapes are matched first, so text like ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ is not italicised.
  • Mentions of you get a stronger highlight; @here/@channel/@everyone always look like they address you.

Toast.tsx and MessageEditor.tsx

Toast.tsx

Toast notifications · 283 lines

A notification stack in the top-right corner for results that finish away from the control that started them, such as a refused reaction or a failed pin. Successes fade after 5 seconds; failures stay until dismissed and can offer a named action like 'Try again' or 'Undo'.

  • useToast() returns show(request), which itself returns a function that removes that toast.
  • At most 4 toasts are visible; a duplicate message and kind replaces the older copy, restarting its timer and re-announcing it.

Optimization: Remaining time is tracked in a ref so pausing and resuming does not restart the 5-second countdown.

MessageEditor.tsx

Inline message editor · 269 lines

The in-place editor shown when you edit one of your messages, with the formatting toolbar, preview, a character counter, and Save/Cancel. Unsaved edits are kept as drafts so they survive restarts, and it detects when the message was changed elsewhere while you were editing.

  • The edit draft is stored under '<channelId>:edit:<messageId>' as JSON { text, base }; older plain-text drafts are still read.

Optimization: Refs (saving, touched, alive) guard against double saves and updates after unmount without extra renders.

ActivityPanel.tsx

Activity (unread/mentions) panel · 259 lines

A side panel listing unread messages or mentions from conversations you joined, with Unread and Mentions tabs, paging, and buttons to jump to a message or mark the conversation read up to it.

  • Loads pages from client.api.activity(mode, { cursor, signal }) through one CoalescedLoader for the panel's life.
  • Switching tab or page clears the list and loads immediately; Refresh and Retry load immediately but keep the current list until the answer.

Admin audit log · 243 lines

A collapsible 'Recent changes' list for admins showing what administrators changed: role changes, deactivations, app tokens, webhooks, invites and so on. Each record is turned into a plain sentence such as 'Sam changed Ana's role from member to admin'.

  • describeAuditEntry maps each audit action to a sentence and looks names up at read time, so renamed people show their current name; your own id reads as 'you'.
  • Detail fields are read defensively, so entries from a newer server produce a shorter sentence instead of 'undefined'.

Optimization: Loads only when opened.

Menu.tsx

Dropdown action menu · 235 lines

A reusable '...' actions menu: a trigger button that opens a floating list of actions, used for rows such as people or channels. It sits on the modal layer, so Escape or clicking outside closes only the menu and focus returns to the trigger.

  • Trigger has aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded; items are role=menuitem with roving focus (tabIndex=-1).
  • Arrow keys move between enabled items with wraparound, Home/End jump to ends, Enter/Space choose, and Tab closes the menu instead of being trapped.

Optimization: Placement and close callbacks are kept in refs, so scroll/resize listeners are attached once.

ProfileDialog.tsx

Profile view and editor · 235 lines

ProfileDialog shows another person's profile (avatar, name, handle, role badge, presence, status) with friend actions and a 'Message <name>' button that opens a direct message. ProfileForm, used in Account settings, lets you edit your own display name and status.

  • 'Message' calls client.openDm([userId]) and hands the new channel id to onOpenDm; failures show a role=alert message.
  • The Message button uses aria-disabled instead of disabled so focus stays on it while it works.
  • ProfileForm saves through client.api.updateMe, falling back to the handle if the display name is blank.

HuddleBar.tsx

Active huddle bar and huddle button · 227 lines

HuddleBar is the strip shown while you are in a huddle: where it is, participant count, faces with a ring for whoever is speaking, the audio player and the controls. HuddleButton is the channel header button that starts or joins a huddle, or shows 'In huddle'.

  • The status line says who is sharing their screen and whether peers are still connecting.
  • Each face shows a green ring when speaking, a mic-off badge when muted and dims while connecting.
  • Offers 'Show video' when the stage is hidden but the call has video (huddleHasVideo).

FormattingToolbar.tsx

Composer formatting bar · 216 lines

The bar above the message box with Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, Inline code, Code block, an emoji search and a Preview toggle. Also exports the shared text-wrapping helper and message length limit used by the composer and the message editor.

  • formatText wraps the selection in a marker, or unwraps it if already wrapped; block mode adds fenced lines with correct newlines.
  • formattingShortcut maps Ctrl+B/I/E to *, _ and .
  • MESSAGE_LIMIT is 12,000 characters.
  • Buttons use onMouseDown preventDefault so clicking them does not steal focus from the textarea.

ViewModal.tsx and WorkspaceStorageGate.tsx

ViewModal.tsx

App-requested form · 192 lines

Renders a form that an installed app (bot/integration) asked to show, with text, select and multi-line fields. The answers are submitted straight back to the app, and any field errors the app returns are shown inline.

  • Reads the current modal from the workspace store; a new view id remounts the form with fresh answers (key={view.id}).
  • Values are keyed by blockId.actionId so two fields sharing an action id in different blocks do not collide.
  • Submits a nested { blockId: { actionId: value } } payload through client.submitModal.

WorkspaceStorageGate.tsx

Workspace address trust gate · 181 lines

A guard that keeps everything that uses locally saved work (drafts, recent searches, queued messages) unmounted until the current server address is trusted for this workspace. If the address is new for a workspace used before, it asks the user to confirm it.

  • Reads self id, workspace id and connection status from the client's Zustand store with useStore.
  • Runs checkWorkspaceAddress on load; 'Trust address and continue' runs trustWorkspaceAddress.
  • The confirmation dialog lists previously trusted addresses beside the one being connected to.

Optimization: Children are not mounted until access is allowed, so storage consumers never run early.

Confirm.tsx and GettingStarted.tsx

Confirm.tsx

Confirmation dialog service · 167 lines

A promise-based 'are you sure?' service: components call useConfirm() and await a yes/no answer for actions that cannot be undone. The provider shows one confirmation dialog at a time with a named action button, never 'OK'.

  • ask() returns a Promise<boolean> that resolves true only when the named action is chosen; Cancel, close and Escape resolve false.
  • A new question resolves any older pending one as false before replacing it.

Optimization: Service object memoised with useMemo and stable useCallback functions, so consumers do not re-render when a dialog opens.

GettingStarted.tsx

Owner onboarding checklist · 167 lines

A small checklist in the sidebar for the workspace owner: create a channel, invite someone, turn on notifications and try a huddle. Each step ticks itself off from what actually happened, and the list hides when all are done or when dismissed.

  • Only shown to the owner role.
  • State (dismissed, huddleTried) is saved per workspace and account on this device via readWorkspaceStorage/writeWorkspaceStorage.
  • 'Create a channel' counts as done when a non-archived channel other than #general exists; 'Invite someone' when any other non-bot active user exists.

Optimization: useMemo for the storage key.

Ctrl+K jump-to switcher · 165 lines

The 'Jump to' dialog opened with Ctrl+K for jumping to any channel, private channel, group conversation or person. Choosing a person with no direct message yet starts one on the server.

Friends list and requests · 164 lines

A dialog for managing friends inside a workspace, with Friends, Requests and Add friends tabs and a name/handle search. Each person row has buttons to add, accept, decline, cancel or remove a friendship.

  • The button label for removal depends on relationship status: Decline (incoming), Cancel request (outgoing) or Remove friend.
  • useTabs supplies accessible tablist/tab/tabpanel props for the three tabs.

DiagnosticsDialog.tsx and HuddleControls.tsx

DiagnosticsDialog.tsx

Diagnostics report · 144 lines

A dialog that builds a plain-text troubleshooting report (app versions, connection status, device and browser details) for the user to copy or save and send to whoever is helping them. Owners and admins also get server health numbers such as sizes, queues and timings. It never includes messages, names or files.

  • Takes one snapshot after client.api.serverInfo() (and workspaceStatus() for admins) answers or fails, so what is shown is exactly what gets copied.
  • Status read failures are explained: 404 means the server version does not report it, 403 means only owners/admins can read it.

HuddleControls.tsx

Huddle control buttons · 141 lines

The mute, camera, screen-share and Leave buttons for a huddle. Shown in the huddle bar and also as an overlay on the full-screen stage.

  • Toggles use aria-pressed for on/off with a fixed aria-label, so screen readers hear the same button before and after pressing.
  • Camera and screen share run through a guarded helper that disables both while busy and turns errors into readable messages via captureFailure.
  • Shows a role=alert with 'Try again' when the microphone is lost (huddle.micLost), calling client.retryMicrophone().
  • overlay mode switches to translucent dark styling for use over video.

ListStatus.tsx and MembersPanel.tsx

ListStatus.tsx

List loading/empty/error status · 141 lines

A shared status area placed above lists that shows loading, failed or empty states. While nothing has loaded it shows placeholder rows shaped like messages; on failure it shows the error with Retry.

  • Kept as one element for the list's whole life so screen readers hear changes in a region they already watch.
  • Retry uses aria-disabled rather than disabled so a focused button does not drop focus during a reload.
  • KeepsFocus uses a layout-effect cleanup to move focus back to the status root when a focused Retry or empty-action button disappears.
  • Placeholder rows pulse only with motion-safe, respecting reduced-motion settings.

MembersPanel.tsx

Channel members side panel · 140 lines

A Discord-style side panel listing who is in the conversation, split into Online and Offline groups with avatars and status text. Clicking a person opens their profile.

  • Uses member ids already on the channel (direct messages) or fetches client.api.channelMembers for channels.
  • Deactivated users are hidden; people are sorted by display name.
  • ListStatus shows loading placeholder rows, errors and a retry button that bumps an attempt counter to refetch.
  • usePanelFocus moves focus to the panel heading when it opens.

Optimization: useMemo for the sorted online/offline split.

ShareableServer.tsx and Icon.tsx

ShareableServer.tsx

Shareable link address provider · 129 lines

A context provider that works out which server address links copied from the app should use (for example a public tunnel address instead of localhost). It also collects every address the current workspace is known by, so links pointing to this workspace can be recognised.

  • Calls client.api.serverInfo() when online, on window focus, when the page becomes visible and every 30 seconds, so a newly opened tunnel is picked up.

Optimization: The context value is memoised on a string of the actual link fields, so frequent hosting-status changes do not re-render every message row (comment cites REV-03).

Icon.tsx

Inline SVG icon set · 127 lines

Tandem's icon set: about 50 single-path SVG icons (search, hash, mic, camera, thread and so on) drawn inline with currentColor. Also exports the BrandMark logo.

  • Icons are a const map of names to SVG path strings on a 24x24 viewBox with round stroke caps.
  • IconName is derived from the map's keys, so names are type-checked.
  • All icons are aria-hidden; the surrounding button supplies the accessible name.
  • Size and stroke width are props (defaults 18px and 1.7).

Optimization: No icon font, network request or runtime dependency: icons are inline paths.
