UI components · 29–30 of 39 smaller files

ShortcutsDialog.tsx and HuddleAudio.tsx

ShortcutsDialog.tsx

Keyboard shortcuts list · 122 lines

A searchable dialog listing Tandem's keyboard shortcuts, grouped as Getting around, Writing and Messages. The Writing list changes depending on whether Enter sends or adds a new line in the user's composer preference.

  • Reads enterSends from useComposerPreferences to choose the right send/new-line keys.
  • Search matches when every typed word appears in the keys or the description.
  • Each key is rendered in its own <kbd> element.
  • An empty result shows a role=status message.

HuddleAudio.tsx

Huddle audio playback · 118 lines

Plays every huddle participant's microphone through hidden audio elements, even when the call has no video. If the browser blocks autoplay, it shows 'Turn on sound', and one click or keypress retries all blocked streams.

  • Each peer gets a PeerAudio component that sets srcObject to the peer's audio stream and calls play().
  • Playback failures are classified: NotAllowedError means a user gesture is needed, AbortError is ignored, anything else is a general failure.

Optimization: register/report are stable useCallback functions, so PeerAudio effects do not re-run on parent renders.

UI components · 31–32 of 39 smaller files

MicrophoneCheck.tsx and NotificationBanner.tsx

MicrophoneCheck.tsx

Microphone test · 105 lines

A 'Test microphone' button for settings that opens the microphone locally and shows a moving level meter, so people can check their mic before a huddle. Nothing is sent anywhere, and the mic closes when the test stops or the component unmounts.

  • Uses testMicrophone and captureFailure from client-core; failures become a readable role=alert message.
  • State machine with phases idle, starting, listening and failed.
  • The meter is a role=meter with aria-valuenow; level is scaled so half the range reads as full.
  • Tells the user if the browser opened the mic but cannot meter it.

NotificationBanner.tsx

Notification permission prompt · 94 lines

A strip shown after sign-in asking the user to turn on browser notifications for mentions. 'Turn on' triggers the browser permission prompt; 'Not now' hides it on this device for 14 days.

  • Only appears while Notification.permission is 'default'; hidden when granted, denied or unsupported.
  • Snooze time is stored through the platform storage abstraction under 'notificationPromptSnoozedAt'.
  • Snoozed state starts as null (unknown) so a snoozed banner never flashes before storage answers.
  • A failed storage write is ignored; the banner still disappears.

UI components · 33–34 of 39 smaller files

MessageAnnouncer.tsx and LazyView.tsx

MessageAnnouncer.tsx

Screen-reader message announcer · 88 lines

A hook that reads newly arrived messages in the open conversation aloud to screen readers through a hidden live log region. The first message is read right away; any arriving during a quiet period are batched into one summary such as '4 new messages, from Ana, Ben and 2 others'.

  • describeHeard truncates single messages to 200 characters and names up to 3 senders before summarising the rest as a count, using Intl.ListFormat.
  • Quiet window defaults to 3000 ms; messages arriving within it wait in a ref and are flushed by one timer.

Optimization: Throttles announcements so a busy channel produces at most one announcement per quiet period.

LazyView.tsx

Lazy-load wrappers · 75 lines

Wrappers for side panels and dialogs whose code is downloaded on first use. They show a 'Loading…' placeholder while the chunk loads and a friendly 'could not load' message with Close and Reload if the download fails.

  • Each wrapper combines an ErrorBoundary (failure fallback) with a React Suspense (loading fallback).
  • LazyPanel's fallbacks are 420px side panels with role=status or role=alert.
  • LazyDialog's fallbacks reuse Dialog, so the loading state already looks like a dialog.

Optimization: Supports code splitting: wraps React.lazy views so their code loads only when first opened.

ReactionPicker.tsx and Avatar.tsx

ReactionPicker.tsx

Emoji reaction picker · 70 lines

A small dialog for reacting with any emoji, not just the six quick reactions. The user types to search, moves through the grid with arrow keys and presses Enter or clicks to pick.

  • findEmoji(query) from lib/emoji supplies matching [emoji, label] pairs.

Avatar.tsx

User avatar and presence dot · 69 lines

Draws a person's avatar as their initials on a colour derived from their user id, plus a small presence dot showing whether they are online. AvatarWithPresence combines both, cutting the dot into the avatar's lower-right corner.

  • Colour comes from avatarColor(user.id) and text from initials(displayName) in lib/format.
  • Font size scales with the avatar size (38% of it).
  • An unknown user shows '?' on the 'lifted' surface colour.
  • PresenceDot is solid green when online and a hollow ring when offline.

UI components · 37–38 of 39 smaller files

ErrorBoundary.tsx and Dialog.tsx

ErrorBoundary.tsx

Render error catcher · 59 lines

Catches a rendering crash in part of the UI and shows a calm 'Something in this screen stopped working' card instead of a blank app. 'Try again' re-renders the same tree without reloading, so the socket connection, loaded history and half-typed drafts survive.

  • Class component using getDerivedStateFromError to store the error and componentDidCatch to log it with the component stack.
  • Accepts an optional fallback node that replaces the default card (used by LazyView).

Optimization: Recovers by resetting state instead of a full page reload, keeping in-memory data.

Dialog.tsx

Standard dialog shell · 53 lines

The common titled dialog box used across the app: a rounded panel near the top of the screen with a heading and a close (X) button. It wraps the lower-level Modal, which handles focus trapping and Escape, and adds the title bar and layout.

  • Delegates focus handling, backdrop and dismissal to Modal with fixed backdrop and panel classes.
  • Width defaults to 440px; height is capped at 80vh with vertical scrolling.
  • dismissible=false disables the close button so a running action cannot be abandoned.

Button.tsx

Button.tsx

Button primitive · 40 lines

Tandem's standard button with four looks: primary, secondary, danger and quiet. It renders a plain native button with Tailwind classes picked from a variant table, and also exports the class builder so links or other elements can look like buttons.

  • VARIANTS maps each variant to a fixed Tailwind class string (copper primary, bordered secondary, red danger, borderless quiet).
  • buttonClass(variant, extra) appends caller layout classes to the variant classes.
  • Keeps the native button's default type, so a Button inside a form still submits unless given type="button".

Area 7 of 14 · packages/ui/test

UI tests

Tests for the shared React UI package run under Vitest with two projects: plain *.test.ts(x) files run in a node environment, and *.dom.test.ts(x) files run in jsdom with setup.ts loaded. Component tests use @testing-library/react and user-event with jest-dom matchers; fake-indexeddb is available for storage tests. Helpers in this folder add an axe-core accessibility check (accessibility.ts), clipboard stand-ins (clipboard.ts), and a fake multi-window device store for race tests (sharedDevice.ts). Coverage spans accessibility and keyboard/focus behaviour of shared widgets, composer and message editing, drafts/outbox persistence across tabs and restarts, notifications and privacy, huddles, desktop hosting, routing, theme tokens, and render-count guards for message rows.

Area 8 of 14 · apps/desktop

Desktop app (Electron)

The Electron desktop app. Its main process can host a full workspace server in-process (the same @slackoss/server the CLI runs), list and back up the workspaces hosted on this computer, publish one to the internet through a Cloudflare tunnel or an externally carried address, and find other workspaces on the LAN over mDNS. A sandboxed, context-isolated renderer loads the shared @slackoss/ui App and talks to the main process only through a small preload bridge, and every IPC request is checked to come from the app's own top-level window. Settings, saved sign-ins (encrypted with the OS key store), drafts and outbox are kept in one JSON file behind a serialized write queue. Most main-process logic is written as plain, Electron-free modules so Vitest can test it directly.

The Electron desktop app. Its main process can host a full workspace server in-process (the same @slackoss/server the CLI runs), list and back up the workspaces hosted on this computer, publish one to the internet through a Cloudflare tunnel or an externally carried address, and find other workspaces on the LAN over mDNS. Desktop · apps/desktop/src/main · part 1 of 3

hosting.ts

Hosting controller · 2,067 lines · changed in 31 commits

createHostingController owns the embedded workspace server's whole lifecycle: starting and stopping workspaces from the registry, renaming, changing ports, backing up, restoring, scheduled backups, starting on launch, and opening the workspace to the internet. Every state-changing operation runs through one serialized queue, and it produces a HostingSnapshot that the window and tray display. It is written against injected callbacks so tests can drive it without Electron.

How it works

  • Returned API: status, list, backupAttention, lastHosted, backup, restore, forget, rename, openFolder, setStartOnLaunch, setReopenPublicOnLaunch, dismissLaunchError, setPort, setAutoBackup, runDueBackups, startForLaunch, networkChanged, start, stop, shutdown, openToAll, endOpenToAll, setInviteOnly, setPublicAddress.
  • All mutations go through serialized(), a promise chain, so start/stop/backup/open requests run one at a time in order.

Optimizations here

  • Single serialized queue avoids races between concurrent requests.
  • Backup retry reservation and exponential backoff stop a crashing backup from retrying expensively on every restart.
  • Free-space check before copying avoids partly written backups.
  • Cleanup timeouts keep quit responsive.

apps/desktop/src/main/hosting.ts (2,067 lines, changed in 31 commits, added 2026-09-13, last changed 2026-10-04). createHostingController owns the embedded workspace server's whole lifecycle: starting and stopping workspaces from the registry, renaming, changing ports, backing up, restoring, scheduled backups, starting on launch, and opening the workspace to the internet. Every state-changing operation runs through one serialized queue, and it produces a HostingSnapshot that the window and tray display. It is written against injected callbacks so tests can drive it without Electron. How it works: - Returned API: status, list, backupAttention, lastHosted, backup, restore, forget, rename, openFolder, setStartOnLaunch, setReopenPublicOnLaunch, dismissLaunchError, setPort, setAutoBackup, runDueBackups, startForLaunch, networkChanged, start, stop, shutdown, openToAll, endOpenToAll, setInviteOnly, setPublicAddress. - All mutations go through serialized(), a promise chain, so start/stop/backup/open requests run one at a time in order. - loadRegistry reads the hosted-workspace list once (strict read), adopts unlisted folders via adoptFolders, and migrates the legacy lastHosted setting only when the registry key is absent. - Starting by { workspaceName } always creates a new folder; { folder } reopens an existing entry; activate puts a restored copy back into normal use. - Restored copies start 'isolated' (loopback only, nothing sent) until activated, and are never backed up or allowed to prune older backups. - backupNow checks the destination exists (never creates it), estimates needed space as folder size x1.1 + 16 MB against free disk, verifies the copy's workspace id, and deletes a copy of the wrong workspace. - Scheduled backups: due every 1 or 7 days (10 min early allowed); a retry slot is reserved before copying; retries back off from 1 hour doubling up to 1 day (max 6 attempts); only one pass runs at a time, with a re-run queued if asked meanwhile. - Failures are classified (destination, space, source, cleanup, other) and kept with the schedule across restarts; pruneBackups keeps the newest 'keep' copies. - openToAll requires a running, non-isolated server with an owner account, sets invite-only (default true) before opening, then sets the public URL, trusts the loopback proxy only for a Tandem-run connector, and adds a Cloudflare STUN server. - A tunnel whose close fails stays owned as cleanupTunnel (TunnelCleanupError) and blocks reopening until stop retries cleanup; closing reverts public URL, ICE servers and proxy trust. - Cleanup steps race a timeout (default 30 s) so a hung stop cannot block quitting forever; system error messages are reduced to their code so paths are not shown. - Snapshot reports LAN URLs, instance id, connected-people count, warnings such as loopback reaching another program (verifyLoopback), launch errors, and public-address config state. Optimizations: - Single serialized queue avoids races between concurrent requests. - Backup retry reservation and exponential backoff stop a crashing backup from retrying expensively on every restart. - Free-space check before copying avoids partly written backups. - Cleanup timeouts keep quit responsive. Desktop · apps/desktop/src/main · part 2 of 3

hosting.ts

Hosting controller · 2,067 lines · changed in 31 commits

How it works (continued)

  • loadRegistry reads the hosted-workspace list once (strict read), adopts unlisted folders via adoptFolders, and migrates the legacy lastHosted setting only when the registry key is absent.
  • Starting by { workspaceName } always creates a new folder; { folder } reopens an existing entry; activate puts a restored copy back into normal use.
  • Restored copies start 'isolated' (loopback only, nothing sent) until activated, and are never backed up or allowed to prune older backups.
  • backupNow checks the destination exists (never creates it), estimates needed space as folder size x1.1 + 16 MB against free disk, verifies the copy's workspace id, and deletes a copy of the wrong workspace.
  • Scheduled backups: due every 1 or 7 days (10 min early allowed); a retry slot is reserved before copying; retries back off from 1 hour doubling up to 1 day (max 6 attempts); only one pass runs at a time, with a re-run queued if asked meanwhile.
  • Failures are classified (destination, space, source, cleanup, other) and kept with the schedule across restarts; pruneBackups keeps the newest 'keep' copies.

Every state-changing operation runs through one serialized queue, and it produces a HostingSnapshot that the window and tray display. It is written against injected callbacks so tests can drive it without Electron. How it works: - Returned API: status, list, backupAttention, lastHosted, backup, restore, forget, rename, openFolder, setStartOnLaunch, setReopenPublicOnLaunch, dismissLaunchError, setPort, setAutoBackup, runDueBackups, startForLaunch, networkChanged, start, stop, shutdown, openToAll, endOpenToAll, setInviteOnly, setPublicAddress. - All mutations go through serialized(), a promise chain, so start/stop/backup/open requests run one at a time in order. - loadRegistry reads the hosted-workspace list once (strict read), adopts unlisted folders via adoptFolders, and migrates the legacy lastHosted setting only when the registry key is absent. - Starting by { workspaceName } always creates a new folder; { folder } reopens an existing entry; activate puts a restored copy back into normal use. - Restored copies start 'isolated' (loopback only, nothing sent) until activated, and are never backed up or allowed to prune older backups. - backupNow checks the destination exists (never creates it), estimates needed space as folder size x1.1 + 16 MB against free disk, verifies the copy's workspace id, and deletes a copy of the wrong workspace. - Scheduled backups: due every 1 or 7 days (10 min early allowed); a retry slot is reserved before copying; retries back off from 1 hour doubling up to 1 day (max 6 attempts); only one pass runs at a time, with a re-run queued if asked meanwhile. - Failures are classified (destination, space, source, cleanup, other) and kept with the schedule across restarts; pruneBackups keeps the newest 'keep' copies. - openToAll requires a running, non-isolated server with an owner account, sets invite-only (default true) before opening, then sets the public URL, trusts the loopback proxy only for a Tandem-run connector, and adds a Cloudflare STUN server. - A tunnel whose close fails stays owned as cleanupTunnel (TunnelCleanupError) and blocks reopening until stop retries cleanup; closing reverts public URL, ICE servers and proxy trust. - Cleanup steps race a timeout (default 30 s) so a hung stop cannot block quitting forever; system error messages are reduced to their code so paths are not shown. - Snapshot reports LAN URLs, instance id, connected-people count, warnings such as loopback reaching another program (verifyLoopback), launch errors, and public-address config state. Optimizations: - Single serialized queue avoids races between concurrent requests. - Backup retry reservation and exponential backoff stop a crashing backup from retrying expensively on every restart. - Free-space check before copying avoids partly written backups. - Cleanup timeouts keep quit responsive.     Desktop · apps/desktop/src/main · part 1 of 3

    index.ts

    Electron main-process entry · 1,187 lines · changed in 52 commits

    Boots the desktop app: enforces a single instance, handles deep links, creates the sandboxed window and tray, registers every IPC handler, browses the LAN for workspaces, and wires the hosting controller to the real embedded server, backup worker and tunnel code. It also owns the quit flow, which makes sure local drafts are saved and hosting is stopped cleanly before exit.

    How it works

    • Keeps the old userData path when renaming the app to Tandem; TANDEM_/GATHERLINE_/SLACKOSS_ env prefixes are all read (e.g. USER_DATA_DIR, TEST, TEST_MEDIA, RELEASE_GATE_REPORT).
    • Every ipcMain.handle goes through guarded() from ipcBoundary.ts, and pushes to the renderer go through appRecipients(), so only the app's own top frame can ask or listen.
    • requestSingleInstanceLock: a second launch hands its tandem:// link to the running instance; macOS links arrive via open-url; links are held in pendingDeepLink until the renderer consumes them.

    Optimizations here

    • Backup/verify/restore run on a worker thread instead of blocking the main thread shared by the window and server.
    • cloudflared path and public-address config cached for 5 seconds; saved public address kept in memory so status snapshots never wait on disk.

    Desktop · apps/desktop/src/main · part 2 of 3

    index.ts

    Electron main-process entry · 1,187 lines · changed in 52 commits

    How it works (continued)

    • Settings storage uses Electron safeStorage; on Linux the basic_text/unknown backends count as unavailable so credentials are never stored in plain text.
    • storage:mergeOutbox / mergeDrafts / mergeRecord merge one window's changes inside the settings queue and push the stored result to the other windows.
    • LAN discovery: bonjour-service browses MDNS_SERVICE_TYPE, prefers IPv4, falls back to linkable IPv6, and publishes the list on lan:servers.
    • Backups, verifies, inventories and restores run in a worker thread via inWorker() (electron-vite ?nodeWorker import) so the window and embedded server stay responsive.
    • startServer calls createWorkspaceServer with the packaged web client path; isolated restored copies bind to 127.0.0.1 with mDNS off; invite-only is forced whenever a stable public address is configured.
    • openTunnel picks between openConfiguredAddress (address carried elsewhere), openNamedTunnel (token file) and openQuickTunnel; cloudflared location and public-address config are re-read at most every 5 seconds.

    More optimizations

    • Background timers (backup schedule, network poll) are unref'd so they never keep the process alive.
    • Single-instance lock avoids running two embedded servers.

    index.ts

    Electron main-process entry · 1,187 lines · changed in 52 commits

    How it works (continued)

    • Window: sandbox + contextIsolation, no nodeIntegration; permissions limited to media, display-capture and notifications from the trusted page; will-navigate blocked; external http(s) links opened in the system browser; screen sharing goes through pickScreen.

    • before-quit: confirm stopping hosting, prepareLocalWrites (renderer save + settings drain), hosting.shutdown(), then quit; on failure the user can keep the app open or force exit.

    Desktop · apps/desktop/src/main · part 1 of 3

    tunnel.ts

    Public address / Cloudflare tunnel · 718 lines · changed in 5 commits

    Everything about reaching a hosted workspace from the internet. It finds cloudflared, opens Cloudflare quick tunnels or token-file named tunnels as a child process, or watches an address something else already carries (Tailscale Funnel, reverse proxy). Every route is confirmed by probing the workspace's /api/health endpoint for this run's instance id before it is published.

    How it works

    • findCloudflared checks TANDEM_/GATHERLINE_/SLACKOSS_CLOUDFLARED, PATH, Program Files, the winget Links folder, and Homebrew/usr paths.
    • launch() strips TUNNEL_* env vars from the child and runs .js/.mjs stand-ins with the app's own executable (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE) for tests.
    • Each cloudflared run gets a temporary config.yml with only no-autoupdate, so a user's ~/.cloudflared/config.yml cannot disable quick tunnels.

    Optimizations here

    • Bounded health-response reads (4 KB) and bounded output buffers.
    • DNS warm-up before the first lookup avoids caching a negative DNS answer.
    • Poll timers are unref'd; consecutive-miss tolerance avoids dropping links on a single blip.

It finds cloudflared, opens Cloudflare quick tunnels or token-file named tunnels as a child process, or watches an address something else already carries (Tailscale Funnel, reverse proxy). Every route is confirmed by probing the workspace's /api/health endpoint for this run's instance id before it is published. How it works: - findCloudflared checks TANDEM_/GATHERLINE_/SLACKOSS_CLOUDFLARED, PATH, Program Files, the winget Links folder, and Homebrew/usr paths. - launch() strips TUNNEL_* env vars from the child and runs .js/.mjs stand-ins with the app's own executable (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE) for tests. - Each cloudflared run gets a temporary config.yml with only no-autoupdate, so a user's ~/.cloudflared/config.yml cannot disable quick tunnels. - Quick tunnels parse the trycloudflare.com URL from output and wait for 'Registered tunnel connection', then a 10 s DNS warm-up, then poll health every 500 ms until it answers as this instance (75 s timeout). - probeHealth adds a random nonce query, disables cache and redirects, times out at 5 s, caps the body at 4 KB, and returns this-workspace / something-else / no-answer. - validatePublicAddress allows only a plain public https origin: no IPs, credentials, path, query, fragment or .local/.lan/.internal-style names. - resolvePublicAddress prefers a saved address, then TANDEM_PUBLIC_URL (carried elsewhere), then TANDEM_TUNNEL_URL + TANDEM_TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE (Tandem-run named tunnel); a half-configured pair is an error, not a silent fallback. - Named tunnels never keep raw cloudflared output, because it can include the token. - openConfiguredAddress polls health every 30 s and gives the address up after 3 misses in a row. - terminate() kills cloudflared, escalates to SIGKILL after 2 s, and throws if the process still can't be confirmed dead; a failed open that can't stop its child rejects with TunnelCleanupError carrying a closable handle. - Output lines are kept to the last 50 and partial lines capped at 16 KB; error text shown to users is shortened to 200 characters. Optimizations: - Bounded health-response reads (4 KB) and bounded output buffers. - DNS warm-up before the first lookup avoids caching a negative DNS answer. - Poll timers are unref'd; consecutive-miss tolerance avoids dropping links on a single blip.     Desktop · apps/desktop/src/main · part 2 of 3

    tunnel.ts

    Public address / Cloudflare tunnel · 718 lines · changed in 5 commits

    How it works (continued)

    • Quick tunnels parse the trycloudflare.com URL from output and wait for 'Registered tunnel connection', then a 10 s DNS warm-up, then poll health every 500 ms until it answers as this instance (75 s timeout).
    • probeHealth adds a random nonce query, disables cache and redirects, times out at 5 s, caps the body at 4 KB, and returns this-workspace / something-else / no-answer.
    • validatePublicAddress allows only a plain public https origin: no IPs, credentials, path, query, fragment or .local/.lan/.internal-style names.
    • resolvePublicAddress prefers a saved address, then TANDEM_PUBLIC_URL (carried elsewhere), then TANDEM_TUNNEL_URL + TANDEM_TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE (Tandem-run named tunnel); a half-configured pair is an error, not a silent fallback.
    • Named tunnels never keep raw cloudflared output, because it can include the token.
    • openConfiguredAddress polls health every 30 s and gives the address up after 3 misses in a row.
    • terminate() kills cloudflared, escalates to SIGKILL after 2 s, and throws if the process still can't be confirmed dead; a failed open that can't stop its child rejects with TunnelCleanupError carrying a closable handle.

How it works: - findCloudflared checks TANDEM_/GATHERLINE_/SLACKOSS_CLOUDFLARED, PATH, Program Files, the winget Links folder, and Homebrew/usr paths. - launch() strips TUNNEL_* env vars from the child and runs .js/.mjs stand-ins with the app's own executable (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE) for tests. - Each cloudflared run gets a temporary config.yml with only no-autoupdate, so a user's ~/.cloudflared/config.yml cannot disable quick tunnels. - Quick tunnels parse the trycloudflare.com URL from output and wait for 'Registered tunnel connection', then a 10 s DNS warm-up, then poll health every 500 ms until it answers as this instance (75 s timeout). - probeHealth adds a random nonce query, disables cache and redirects, times out at 5 s, caps the body at 4 KB, and returns this-workspace / something-else / no-answer. - validatePublicAddress allows only a plain public https origin: no IPs, credentials, path, query, fragment or .local/.lan/.internal-style names. - resolvePublicAddress prefers a saved address, then TANDEM_PUBLIC_URL (carried elsewhere), then TANDEM_TUNNEL_URL + TANDEM_TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE (Tandem-run named tunnel); a half-configured pair is an error, not a silent fallback. - Named tunnels never keep raw cloudflared output, because it can include the token. - openConfiguredAddress polls health every 30 s and gives the address up after 3 misses in a row. - terminate() kills cloudflared, escalates to SIGKILL after 2 s, and throws if the process still can't be confirmed dead; a failed open that can't stop its child rejects with TunnelCleanupError carrying a closable handle. - Output lines are kept to the last 50 and partial lines capped at 16 KB; error text shown to users is shortened to 200 characters. Optimizations: - Bounded health-response reads (4 KB) and bounded output buffers. - DNS warm-up before the first lookup avoids caching a negative DNS answer. - Poll timers are unref'd; consecutive-miss tolerance avoids dropping links on a single blip.     Desktop app (Electron) · 1–2 of 19 smaller files

    registry.ts and platform.ts

    registry.ts

    Hosted-workspace registry · 378 lines

    Defines how the list of workspaces hosted on this computer is stored in settings, and parses it defensively. It also reads a workspace's id and name straight from its SQLite file without starting a server, writes a rename into a stopped workspace's database, and adopts workspace folders that the list does not yet name.

    • Registry is { version: 1, workspaces: [...] }; a newer or unknown version throws RegistryFormatError instead of being treated as empty.
    • Folder names must match /^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$/ so a hand-edited entry cannot point outside the hosted folder; new folders are w-<uuid>.

    platform.ts

    Electron Platform adapter · 240 lines

    electronPlatform() implements the UI's Platform interface on top of the preload bridge: storage, notifications, LAN discovery, deep links and every hosting call. followPlace() reports the page's URL and history state to the main process so crash recovery can restore it.

    • plainly() strips Electron's "Error invoking remote method '...':" prefix so users see the main process's own message.
    • onPrepareClose runs all 'capture' handlers, then all 'persist' handlers, then acknowledges with saved true/false.

    Optimization: Debounces place reports (250 ms) so scrolling does not flood IPC.

    Desktop app (Electron) · 3–4 of 19 smaller files

    settings.ts and index.ts

    settings.ts

    Settings file storage · 142 lines

    createSettingsStorage stores all desktop settings in one JSON file and runs every read and write through a single promise queue. Writes are atomic (temp file, fsync, rename), saved sign-ins are always stored encrypted, and legacy plain-text sign-ins are migrated the first time they are read.

    • API: get (with strict and distinguishMissing options), set, update (read-modify-write in one queue turn), drain.
    • Temp file opened with mode 0o600, written, synced, then renamed over the real file.

    Optimization: Atomic write with fsync protects against partial files after a crash.

    index.ts

    Preload bridge · 138 lines

    Exposes window.slackoss to the sandboxed renderer through contextBridge. Each method is a thin ipcRenderer.invoke call or a listener subscription that returns an unsubscribe function; no Node APIs are exposed.

    • Storage: storageGet/Set/Initialize, storageMergeOutbox/Drafts/Record and their change listeners.
    • LAN: lanSnapshot and onLanServers.
    • Hosting: status, list, start, stop, backup, restore, rename, setPort, setAutoBackup, openToAll, setPublicAddress, open-at-login and more.
    • Window: deep links, revealWindow, rememberPlace/takePlace for crash recovery, onPrepareClose/preparedClose for the close handshake.

    Desktop app (Electron) · 5–6 of 19 smaller files

    credentials.ts and ipcBoundary.ts

    credentials.ts

    Saved sign-in encryption · 127 lines

    Validates and encrypts the list of saved workspace sign-ins using a CredentialProtector (Electron safeStorage in production). It refuses to fall back to plain text when the OS key store is locked, and its errors never echo the credential contents.

    • Encrypted envelope: { kind: 'gatherline.saved-servers', version: 1, ciphertext: base64 } (name kept from the old brand so older files still read).
    • Each server URL must be http(s) with no credentials, query or hash; tokens must be non-empty.
    • Base64 is validated strictly and must round-trip.
    • decodeSavedServers still accepts legacy plain arrays so the settings layer can migrate them.

    ipcBoundary.ts

    IPC trust boundary · 117 lines

    Decides which IPC requests the main process will answer and which windows hear its pushes. Only the live main window's top frame, showing the app's own page (same origin and path), qualifies, and a refused request gets a generic message that names nothing.

    • rendererUrlTrust compares origin and pathname only, so hash and query can change.
    • fromTrustedWindow checks sender id, that the frame has no parent, and that processId/routingId match the window's main frame.
    • guarded wraps a handler and throws REFUSED before any work starts.

    Desktop app (Electron) · 7–8 of 19 smaller files

    rendererRecovery.ts and closePreparation.ts

    rendererRecovery.ts

    Renderer crash recovery · 111 lines

    Policy for when the window's page crashes or fails to load: reload up to 3 times per minute after a 500 ms pause, then ask the user. PlaceCheckpoint remembers where the page was (URL and history state) so a recovered page reopens the same conversation, thread and panel.

    • isRendererLoadFailure ignores sub-frames and ERR_ABORTED (-3).
    • PlaceCheckpoint only accepts trusted URLs and states up to 32 KB of JSON, and hands the saved state back once.
    • reset() starts a fresh count after the user chooses Try again.

    Optimization: Bounded reload loop avoids a window that reloads forever.

    closePreparation.ts

    Close/quit handshake · 86 lines

    ClosePreparation coordinates closing: it asks the renderer to save its final work, waits for an acknowledgement, then drains the settings queue. It times out after 10 seconds by default and reports failure so the app can ask the user instead of losing drafts.

    • prepare(windowId, send, drain) returns a shared promise if a preparation is already pending.
    • acknowledge checks the window id, request id and a boolean 'saved' before accepting.
    • With no window, it skips straight to draining settings.
    • Late replies cannot complete a newer attempt because each request has its own id.

    Release-gate self-report · 51 lines

    Desktop app (Electron) · 11–12 of 19 smaller files

    backupWorker.ts and loginItem.ts

    backupWorker.ts

    Backup worker thread · 47 lines

    A worker_threads entry that runs exactly one backup, verify, inventory or restore job and posts back the result or an error message. It imports only the server's backup module, not the server barrel, so the worker does not load Fastify or sockets.

    • Job kinds: backup (dataDir, out), verify (dir), inventory (dir), restore (backupDir, dataDir).
    • Reads the job from workerData and replies once through parentPort; errors are reduced to their message.
    • The comment notes a 200,000-message backup held the main thread about two thirds of a second before this move.

    Optimization: Moves long synchronous SQLite work (VACUUM INTO, integrity_check) off the main thread.

    loginItem.ts

    Open-at-login rules · 40 lines

    Platform rules for starting Tandem when the user signs in. Windows passes a --hidden argument; macOS instead reports wasOpenedAtLogin. It also turns a registration that did not take into a message the user can act on.

    • Only Windows gets args on the login item.
    • macOS 'requires-approval' status produces a message pointing to System Settings > Login Items.

    mergeDraftsSetting does for drafts what the outbox helper does for queued sends: it merges a window's draft changes in one settings-queue turn so a draft typed in one window is not lost to another.

    The HTML page the desktop window loads. It sets a strict Content-Security-Policy matching the one the server sends (minus frame-ancestors), and mounts src/main.tsx.

    Web app · 1–2 of 4 smaller files

    precompress.ts and index.html

    precompress.ts

    Precompression Vite plugin · 80 lines

    After a build, walks the output folder and writes a Brotli (.br) and gzip (.gz) copy next to each compressible text file over 1 KB. Copies are kept only if smaller than the original, and maximum compression settings are used since this runs once at build time (REV-13).

    • Compressible extensions: .html, .js, .mjs, .css, .svg, .json, .txt, .map.
    • Brotli uses text mode, max quality and a size hint; gzip uses best compression.
    • Both compressions run in parallel per file.
    • Plugin applies only to builds and runs in writeBundle.

    Optimization: Precompressed Brotli and gzip assets so the server never compresses per request.

    index.html

    HTML shell · 19 lines

    The browser client's HTML page with a meta description, dark theme color, the SVG favicon, and the module script for src/main.tsx.

    • Mount point is div#root.

    Area 11 of 14 · .github

    Build, CI and release

    The pnpm + Turborepo monorepo setup, the shared TypeScript and formatting config, the Docker image, the GitHub Actions workflows, and the scripts that act as gates. A shared build-identity system hashes each artifact's source inputs and writes build.json beside every build, so tests and releases refuse anything not built from the checkout. CI is designed around a small free-minutes budget: path-filtered workflows, Turbo task caching, separate cache-filling on main, and artifact cleanup. Gates check web bundle size, precompressed assets, the desktop archive's contents, Turbo cache inputs, and release manifests.

    Build, CI and release · 1–2 of 11 smaller files

    seed-demo.mjs and build-identity.mjs

    seed-demo.mjs

    Demo data seeder · 358 lines

    Fills an empty workspace through the public REST API with four people, channels with topics, a thread, reactions, a mention, a pinned checklist, an image, statuses and a direct message. It refuses a workspace that already has accounts.

    • Usage: node scripts/seed-demo.mjs [address] [--password] [--claim-code]; default http://localhost:8543.
    • Generates a shared password unless one is given and prints it at the end.
    • Builds a mockup PNG in code (zlib deflate + crc32) for the image upload.

    build-identity.mjs

    Build identity and staleness check · 292 lines

    Computes which source an artifact was built from: version, git revision, whether the tree was dirty, and a 16-hex hash of all input files' paths and bytes. Builds write this as build.json, and 'check' compares built artifacts (including inside the desktop asar) against the checkout, failing with the command to rebuild.

    • SHARED_INPUTS = package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, turbo.json's globalDependencies and this script, so anything that makes Turbo rebuild also makes old builds stale.
    • ARTIFACTS lists inputs for web, server and desktop and the rebuild command for each.

    Optimization: Content hash works without .git, so container builds identify themselves too.

    Build, CI and release · 3–4 of 11 smaller files

    release-manifest.mjs and check-ci-cache.mjs

    release-manifest.mjs

    Release manifest and binding · 257 lines

    'bind' records the SHA-256 of files a tested build staged. The main command checks every artifact's build.json names the release commit, a clean tree and the tag's version, that exactly one server archive and one installer were staged and are unchanged, and that the server tarball carries the same identity. It then writes SHA256SUMS and release notes.

    • Tags must be v1.2.3 or v1.2.3-rc.1; revision must be a 40-hex commit.
    • readTarGzFile extracts build.json from the server tar.gz without external tools.
    • Notes include a table of artifact, version, revision and inputs hash, and a SmartScreen warning when unsigned.

    check-ci-cache.mjs

    Turbo cache-input gate · 235 lines

    Copies the tracked workspace into a temporary git repo and uses 'turbo run --dry=json' to prove that editing specific files changes exactly the task hashes it should and leaves unrelated ones alone. This catches turbo.json input mistakes that would make CI reuse stale results or rebuild too much.

    • Expects 15 tasks (7 typechecks, 5 tests, 3 builds) and stable hashes across repeated dry runs.
    • Checks VITEST_MAX_THREADS/FORKS change only test hashes and add no CLI arguments.

    Optimization: Protects the correctness of CI's Turbo cache.

    release-install-gates.ps1 and check-desktop-archive.mjs

    release-install-gates.ps1

    Windows installer gates · 159 lines

    PowerShell script run on a disposable Windows runner: silently installs the new installer, launches the app and checks it registers its URL schemes and reports the expected profile, upgrades over the previous release and proves the new version reads the old profile's marker, then uninstalls and checks user data remains.

    • Parameters: -Installer, -Version, optional -Previous and -Revision.
    • Finds the install via the per-user Uninstall registry key (accepts the older Gatherline name).
    • Uses TANDEM_RELEASE_GATE_REPORT to get the app's own report of which userData it uses.

    check-desktop-archive.mjs

    Desktop archive gate · 139 lines

    check-web-precompressed.mjs and desktop-ci-mode.mjs

    check-web-precompressed.mjs

    Precompression gate · 96 lines

    Checks every compressible file over 1 KB in a built client has both .br and .gz copies, that each decodes to exactly the original, and that no copy is orphaned. Prints the total savings.

    • Mirrors the extension list and size threshold in apps/web/precompress.ts.
    • Fails if there is nothing to compress (not a built client).

    Optimization: Guarantees precompressed assets match what is served (REV-13).

    desktop-ci-mode.mjs

    Desktop CI mode selector · 59 lines

    Decides whether the desktop workflow must build the NSIS installer or only the unpacked app, by diffing the PR against its base. Installer coverage is kept whenever packaging inputs change or the diff cannot be computed.

    • Installer inputs: any package.json, lockfile, workspace/npm config, electron-builder.yml, apps/desktop/build/, the icon script, this script and the workflow.
    • Manual runs default to the installer.
    • Writes installer=true|false to GITHUB_OUTPUT.

    Optimization: Skips the slow installer build on runtime-only changes.

One Ubuntu job runs formatting, automation typecheck, the cache-input gate, unit tests of the gate scripts, Turbo typecheck/test/build with a restored task cache, bundle-size and precompression gates, and the web Playwright suite. A follow-up job deletes Actions artifacts left by earlier runs. .github/workflows/container.yml: Builds the Docker image and runs the smoke and layer-reuse tests, only when files that go into the image change. Layers are cached in the GitHub Actions cache under one scope. .github/workflows/desktop.yml: On Windows, packages the desktop app and runs the archive, bundle-size and precompression gates, then the desktop Playwright suite. It builds only the unpacked app for ordinary runtime changes and adds the NSIS installer when installer inputs change or on manual runs.

    docker/Dockerfile: Multi-stage build of the bundled server plus web client into a small node:24-alpine runtime image. Dependencies are fetched from the lockfile alone in their own stage, so source edits reuse that layer. The final image runs as a non-root user with a /data volume, a health check, and mDNS disabled. package.json: Root of the pnpm workspace (pnpm 10.23, Node >= 24). Its scripts fan out through Turbo for dev/build/typecheck/test and run Playwright for the web and desktop end-to-end suites. playwright.config.ts: Playwright config for tests/e2e/web.spec.ts: one worker, headless Chromium at 1280x820 with fake mic/camera, screenshots and traces kept on failure. A global setup refuses to run unless the server build matches the checkout. playwright.desktop.config.ts: Playwright config for tests/e2e/desktop.spec.ts, which launches the packaged Windows app. A global setup checks the packaged build matches the checkout. pnpm-workspace.yaml: Declares packages/* and apps/* as workspace packages, and allows install scripts only for electron, electron-winstaller and esbuild. tsconfig.automation.json: Type-checks the files that belong to no workspace package: the Playwright configs, tests/e2e and scripts/*.mts. CI runs it early so a type error fails before expensive steps. tsconfig.base.json: Strict ES2023/ESNext settings with bundler module resolution shared by every package. Enables noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax and isolatedModules, and emits declarations and source maps.

    Area 12 of 14 · tests

    Benchmarks and end-to-end tests

    Measurement scripts under scripts/measure-* run real workspace servers on seeded data to time specific hot paths (search, snapshots, unread counts, thread indexing, publication fan-out, event-loop stalls, client load and scroll, desktop start) and report medians and percentiles, so two revisions can be compared. Each checks its fixture before timing, so errors are never reported as speed. The tests/ folder holds the Playwright end-to-end suites for the browser client and the packaged Windows app, the Docker smoke and layer-reuse checks, and a fake cloudflared used by tunnel tests.

    Benchmarks and end-to-end tests · 1–2 of 10 smaller files

    measure-mixed.mts and measure-client.mts

    measure-mixed.mts

    Mixed-workload benchmark · 570 lines

    A repeatable mixed load on one server: posting in several channels, searching, devices dropping and reconnecting, and maintenance running at once. It verifies every post reaches every connected device, reconnects get exactly the missed events, and retention removes exactly the expired data, then reports p50/p95/p99, event-loop delay and memory to a JSON artifact.

    • Options: --seed, --people, --devices, --history, --rounds, --seconds, --expired, --out.
    • Uses Node's built-in WebSocket and monitorEventLoopDelay.

    Optimization: Event-loop delay and memory tracking under load.

    measure-client.mts

    Client load/scroll benchmark · 425 lines

    Runs the built web client in headless Chromium against an in-process server seeded with history and pictures. It times cold and warm first usable conversation (with bytes and requests), and scrolling a picture channel back to its first message, recording long tasks, slow frames and JS heap.

    • Options: --seed, --history, --pictures, --rounds, --out; CHROMIUM env to choose a browser.
    • Verifies the web build is fresh via build-identity check().

    Optimization: Measures cold vs warm HTTP cache load, long tasks and heap growth.

    measure-stall.mts and measure-unread-counts.mts

    measure-stall.mts

    Event-loop stall benchmark · 297 lines

    Measures how long database work blocks the event loop that the desktop window shares with its embedded server. Seeds 50,000 messages and times the longest stall during reading, searching, concurrent readers, the scheduled queue, backups, startup and retention, including a backup run on a worker thread for comparison.

    • --messages (default 50000).
    • Uses measure-stall-worker.mts through node:worker_threads with tsx registered.

    Optimization: Quantifies the benefit of running backups on a worker thread.

    Tandem codebase tour · Optimizations

    258 / 340

    The approach

    Measure first, then fix, then lock it in with a test

    Tandem began on 31 August 2026 as a feature-complete Slack-like stack. Its optimization work then followed a measure-first discipline: every performance change ships with a reproducible harness in scripts/measure-*.mts, before/after numbers recorded in docs, and a regression test that pins the mechanism. The first wave (5-29 September) set hard bounds on memory and work: a 300-message timeline window, LRU history and file caches, streamed files, a 2 MiB slow-socket cutoff, rate limiting, a bounded scheduled queue and a 500 kB entry-bundle guard enforced in CI. The OPT series (30 September-1 October) then targeted measured SQLite hot paths. A composite thread index, a mentions table, batched snapshot queries and a windowed common-word search each cut a 200,000-message workload by 4-50x. The REV/F series (2-3 October) addressed fan-out and delivery costs, React re-render churn, Electron worker and package size, and Brotli precompression. That series also contained many lifecycle and data-safety failures, and the 4 October N01-N12 pass continued it. Larger architectural experiments are still open in the plans and are not claimed as done: isolating the embedded server, list virtualization, lean bootstrap, compile cache and media thumbnails.

    Tandem codebase tour · Optimizations

    260 / 340

    Client state & rendering: Message rows subscribe only to what they render; Stable hosting link context; Untouched open threads keep their references; Coalesced Activity refreshes; Cancel unneeded history loads; share identical ones; Bounded ephemeral (private) command answers; 300-message timeline window with anchored paging; LRU-bounded inactive conversation and thread caches; Viewport-only image previews, 4 transfers, 32 MiB idle LRU; Cached attachments released with their message; Streamed uploads/downloads and native large-file handoff; Memoized rows and a separate draft-persistence subscriber Reliability & data safety: Retention purges by message count through a temp table; Fair, backed-off attachment removal queue; Integrity-check rollback copies before pruning; One server process per workspace folder; Post-commit failures cannot cut off durable events; Background queues and socket callbacks contained; Close/quit waits for drafts, outbox and settings; Outbox persisted as soon as a send is accepted; Outbox tombstones compacted behind a durable floor; Web device storage in IndexedDB with a write journal Real-time delivery: Read a change's audience once per publication (F10); One membership check and body per app event (F11); No member reads or recounts for offline recipients; Authorize each session once per fan-out; App events delivered through a pump; Retry given-up app events only as room frees; Durable, bounded outgoing integration queue; 2 MiB WebSocket queued-byte cutoff with durable replay Database & queries: Composite (thread_root_id, id) index for thread pages; message_mentions table for unread mention counts; Handshake snapshot no longer grows with every member; Common-word search walks a newest-first window; Filename search reads matching rows as one list (F13); Bounded per-zone date formatters for search; Scheduled queue: admission caps, 10-row drain, held-row backoff Bundle & startup: Minified desktop renderer; Lazy panels, side-effect-free protocol, 500 kB CI guard; Hosting dialog, video stage and form dialogs on first use; Keep zod out of the first bundle; Join screen and two dialogs loaded on first use; Brotli/gzip precompressed client and immutable hashed assets Build & CI: Turbo task cache, build reuse and unpacked Windows packaging; Stop hoarding CI artifacts; Docker dependency layer reused across source edits; Load-sensitive test timeouts fixed; Reproducible performance harnesses and mixed baseline; Build identity and stale-artifact refusal Desktop & Electron: Backup, verify and restore on a worker thread; Backup worker loads only the backup module; Dependency TypeScript sources left out of the desktop archive; Desktop archive content gate; Bounded renderer crash and failed-load recovery Security: Bounded concurrent scrypt derivations; Per-caller token-bucket rate limits; Content security policy and credential-free logs; IPC answered only from the main window's top frame; Patched vulnerable runtime dependencies

    Tandem codebase tour · Optimizations

    261 / 340

    No member reads or recounts for offline recipients: On a 50-member channel, deleting a 21-message thread with nobody connected: 1,050 -> 0 recounts (21 -> 0 member reads). With two connected: 1,050 -> 2. A plain message: 1 -> 0 member reads. Source: docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN-2026-10-02.md REV-06 slice A. Stable hosting link context: 30 MessageItem rows, each in its own Profiler: a connected-count change rendered 30 -> 0 rows, while a real address change still renders all 30. Source: docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN-2026-10-02.md REV-03. Untouched open threads keep their references: With 20 open threads of 300 replies, an event outside every thread changed 20 -> 0 threads. Source: docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN-2026-10-02.md REV-03. Outbox persisted as soon as a send is accepted: In the two-window race, before: [accepted by A] -> []. After: the send is kept and delivered on the next start. Sources: docs/CODE-AUDIT-AND-EXECUTION-PLAN-2026-09-27.md (R143-C1) and docs/UPDATE-PLAN-2026-09-30.md (FIX-01). Patched vulnerable runtime dependencies: Production audit 6 high + 4 moderate -> 0, and full audit 13 high -> 0. Later reviews report zero known vulnerabilities.     Client state & rendering · 5 of 12 · 2026-10-02

    Cancel unneeded history loads; share identical ones

    Layer: client-core

    The problem

    Two equivalent initial history loads made 2 real HTTP requests, and neither was aborted when the client was destroyed.

    The change

    Each timeline and thread load carries an AbortController that is stopped on supersession, eviction, reset or destroy. An identical in-flight request, including identical newer pages (F14), is joined instead of repeated.

    api.ts

    Cached attachments released with their message

    Layer: client-core

    The problem

    Deleted, revoked or retention-purged attachments stayed in the client file cache, and in-flight transfers could reinstall them.

    Streamed uploads/downloads and native large-file handoff

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Files could pass through memory as whole buffers, and large downloads became a full JavaScript blob before saving.

    The change

    Uploads pipe to disk and downloads stream from a file handle, keeping only the first 64 KiB for image dimensions. Files of 8 MiB or more go through the browser or Electron download manager using single-use 60-second hashed tickets (schema v19).

    Reliability & data safety · 1 of 10 · 2026-09-29

    Retention purges by message count through a temp table

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Retention bounded work by thread roots, so one huge thread produced a single statement with too many SQL variables, and the sweep failed.

    The change

    The purge goes through a temp table in passes of 5,000 messages, with a yielding 30 s sweep, caught timer steps and retentionStatus().

    store.ts

    server.ts

    How it is verified

    1 root plus 33,000 replies: the old code failed with 'too many SQL variables'. It is now purged in one pass. Source: docs/UPDATE-PLAN-2026-09-30.md, FIX-05.

    Reliability & data safety · 2 of 10 · 2026-10-02

    Fair, backed-off attachment removal queue

    Layer: server

    The problem

    A page of 100 failing unlink paths starved healthy deletions. A real 21-byte upload stayed stuck through three flushes and a restart.

    The change

    Schema v35 gives each pending removal its attempt count, next attempt time and queue time. Failures back off over 1 min, 5 min, 30 min and then 2 h while the others proceed. A full page continues on the next turn.

    Reliability & data safety · 4 of 10 · 2026-09-30

    One server process per workspace folder

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Two servers could open the same SQLite workspace (through the same path, a symlink or a '..' spelling) and corrupt each other's state.

    The change

    An OS-level SQLite lock on workspace.lock plus an owner note. A second start is refused, and restore, recovery and the desktop rename hold the lock.

    ownership.ts

    ownership.test.ts

    How it is verified

    Of three servers started at once, one runs. After the holder is killed with SIGKILL, the next start succeeds. Source: docs/UPDATE-PLAN-2026-09-30.md, FIX-11.

    Reliability & data safety · 5 of 10 · 2026-10-02

    Post-commit failures cannot cut off durable events

    Layer: server

    The problem

    A failed recount after a committed DELETE returned 500 and stopped the remaining deletion frames, so clients kept showing deleted content after reconnecting.

    The change

    Every post-commit step (access effects, each durable frame, follow states, counts) fails on its own. A frame that cannot be fanned out closes every socket (1012), so clients replay from their last event.

    server.ts

    gateway.ts

    How it is verified

    Server socket tests plus a real-client reconnect test. The deep review had reproduced 4 durable deletions with only 1 delivered and 0 replayed. Source: docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN-2026-10-02.md REV-10 and docs/research/2026-10-02-deep/README.md.

    A Store read error in the scheduler, event delivery or attachment timers made the host process exit with code 1. Gateway socket callbacks were similarly unguarded.

    The change

    Every timer, immediate and startup entry runs through one contained runner that logs, counts, keeps durable rows and retries next round. backgroundFailures appears in admin status. Gateway message, heartbeat, close and upgrade callbacks are contained (F03).

    Reliability & data safety · 9 of 10 · 2026-09-30

    Outbox tombstones compacted behind a durable floor

    Layer: client-core

    The problem

    Tombstones were compacted by count, so a stale window could resurrect deleted sends, and purged messages lost their send keys.

    The change

    Reliability & data safety · 10 of 10 · 2026-10-02

    Web device storage in IndexedDB with a write journal

    Layer: ui

    The problem

    localStorage gives no acknowledged cross-tab transactions, so drafts, outbox and preferences could be lost or overwritten across tabs and crashes.

    The change

    Each change is one IndexedDB transaction serialized across tabs. A small localStorage journal is replayed on the next start if the page died, and per-key change IDs ensure a replay never overwrites newer data. An open failure reports unreadability rather than switching to an empty store (N02).

    Real-time delivery · 7 of 8 · 2026-09-11

    Durable, bounded outgoing integration queue

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Outgoing events were fire-and-forget. Once made durable, a dead endpoint's queue grew without limit, and each event spent an 8-hour retry ladder.

    The change

    Schema v20 queues events in the same transaction as the workspace event. Delivery is ordered per subscription, runs 10 endpoints in parallel, and retries up to 8 attempts. Schema v21 caps each endpoint at 500 waiting events, counts drops visibly, and gives up a dead endpoint's backlog together.

    store.ts

    Composite (thread_root_id, id) index for thread pages

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Thread pagination read old threads through idx_messages_channel and scanned every newer unrelated message in the channel. The newest page of an old thread cost about 92 ms at 200,000 messages.

    Handshake snapshot no longer grows with every member

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Each listed channel ran its own manager query, which read every member row because is_manager had no index. Presence also listed every account as offline. After a restart every client reconnects and builds a snapshot at once, so this cost scaled badly.

    The change

    Database & queries · 4 of 7 · 2026-10-01

    Common-word search walks a newest-first window

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Every search took all of its FTS matches, joined and filtered them, then sorted them all to return 20 rows. A word in 60% of 200,000 messages cost 122 ms per page.

    The change

    A cheap count stops at 5,001 matches. Above that threshold the newest 20,000 in-scope messages (Store.SEARCH_WINDOW) are checked against their own matches first, and older messages are read from the matches only if the window holds less than a page.

Source: docs/OPTIMIZATION-PLAN-2026-09-30.md OPT-11.     Database & queries · 7 of 7 · 2026-09-29

    Scheduled queue: admission caps, 10-row drain, held-row backoff

    Layer: server

    The problem

    2,000 due scheduled messages drained in one synchronous pass that stalled the event loop for about 3 s. Every held row was also re-checked on every 15-second tick.

    The change

    Scheduling is capped at 200 outstanding per account and 10,000 per workspace. flushScheduled sends batches of 10 and yields with setImmediate between them. Held rows get next_attempt_at (schema v27) and are woken when their obstacle clears.

    Build & CI · 1 of 6 · 2026-10-01

    Turbo task cache, build reuse and unpacked Windows packaging

    Layer: build

    The problem

    CI rebuilt the web client in several phases, started every Vitest pool at once, and built an unused NSIS installer on ordinary PRs.

    The change

    Turbo builds, typechecks and tests with a .turbo/cache archive keyed by OS, Node, lockfile and commit. Concurrency is capped at 2 with 2 Vitest workers. Ordinary PRs package with --win --dir, and check-ci-cache.mjs verifies cache inputs (15 mutations, 101 assertions).

    CI.md

    check-ci-cache.mjs

    desktop-ci-mode.mjs

    ci.yml

    Bound

    1.09 s warm repeat

    An identical local repeat restored every task from cache in 1.09 s. The ordinary PR skips the 73-89 s installer stage, and unpacked packaging took 57.65 s locally. Remote Actions timings are not yet measured. Source: docs/CI.md.

    Desktop & Electron · 5 of 5 · 2026-10-02

    Bounded renderer crash and failed-load recovery

    Layer: desktop

    The problem

    A crashed or failed renderer left a dead window, and load promises were discarded unhandled.

    The change

    On render-process-gone or a main-frame did-fail-load, the window reloads its own address after 0.5 s, up to 3 failures a minute, then offers Try again or Quit. F08 restores the same place in history.

    rendererRecovery.ts

    index.ts

    How it is verified

    A packaged journey crashes the page four times and finds Saved messages open again each time. Sources: docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN-2026-10-02.md REV-09 and the FOLLOWUP F08.

    Security · 1 of 5 · 2026-09-05

    Bounded concurrent scrypt derivations

    Layer: server

    The problem

    scrypt is memory-hard, so unbounded concurrent logins were a memory-exhaustion attack that also stalled chat.

    The change

    At most two derivations run at once, and the rest get 429.

    server.ts

    auth.ts

    Bound

    2 concurrent derivations

    Documented in docs/VALIDATION.md, 'Memory work behind those numbers'. The mechanism is at server.ts ('Bound simultaneous password derivations').

    Security · 2 of 5 · 2026-09-12

    Per-caller token-bucket rate limits

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Nothing bounded how often a caller could sign in, post, upload, open sockets or send typing notices.

    The change

    Token buckets are keyed by account, or by address only for sign-in and socket open, with a tight per-handle failed-login bucket. Refusals return 429 with Retry-After, and buckets are dropped once refilled. Webhooks and app callouts were later admitted the same way.

    limits.ts

    limits.test.ts

    How it is verified

    Covered by packages/server/test/limits.test.ts. The posting burst is 60 so an outbox catching up is not refused. Source: docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN-2026-09.md, 'Rationing what one caller can do'.

    Tandem codebase tour · Optimizations

    Security · 3 of 5 · 2026-09-12

    Content security policy and credential-free logs

    Layer: server

    The problem

    Message markup had no script-src barrier, and tokens in URLs could reach request logs and Referer headers.

    The change

    script-src 'self', no objects, no base rewrite and no framing on every response, mirrored in the desktop renderer HTML. Referrer-Policy is no-referrer, and the request logger redacts credentials (with N01 hardening against malformed query names).

    securityHeaders.ts

    redact.ts

    How it is verified

    A test fails if the server and desktop policies disagree. The browser suite notices CSP violations. Sources: docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN-2026-09.md, 'A content security policy for both clients', and docs/IMPLEMENTATION-2026-10-04.md (N01).

    Security · 4 of 5 · 2026-10-01

    IPC answered only from the main window's top frame

    Layer: desktop

    The problem

    Any window or frame with the preload could call storage and hosting IPC, and main-process pushes went to every window.

    The change

    Every ipcMain.handle goes through ipcBoundary.ts, which checks the live main window, top frame and app origin and validates storage keys. Pushes go only to the app's own window (F09).

    ipcBoundary.ts

    index.ts

    How it is verified

    A packaged journey opens a foreign window with the app's preload. It is refused storage and hosting and hears none of the primary window's draft, outbox or record changes. Sources: docs/IMPROVEMENT-PLAN-2026-10-02.md REV-14 and the FOLLOWUP F09.
